SUMMARY
This summary provides an overview of the information contained in this Prospectus and does not
include all information that may be important to you. It should be read together with, and is qualified in
its entirety by, the full text of this Prospectus. We incurred losses in each year during the Track Record
Period, and there can be no assurance that we will be able to achieve or sustain profitability in the
future. You should read this Prospectus in full before making an investment decision. Investing in the
OfferSharesinvolvesrisks,whicharedescribedin“RiskFactors.”Certaintermsusedinthissectionare
definedin“Definitions”and“GlossaryofTechnicalTermsandConventions.”
OVERVIEW
WhoWeAre
We are a leading autonomous driving company in terms of both technological advancement and
commercial success. We ranked No. 1 among all independent driving automation solutions providers
globally in terms of both the sales volume of vehicles equipped with our Urban NOA solutions for the
trailing 12 months ended February 28, 2026, and the number of mass-produced vehicle models
incorporating our Urban NOA solutions as of February 28, 2026, according to CIC. According to CIC, in
2025,wewereamongthetopfiveplayersinChina’sL2assisteddrivingsolutionsmarket,whichconsistsof
L2-Urban NOA, L2-Highway NOA and conventional ADAS solutions, and among the top ten players
globallyinthesamemarket.Wefocusondevelopingandcommercializingdrivingautomationtechnologies
to improve safety and efficiency in mobility and logistics, including through mass-produced vehicle
solutions and scalable autonomous mobility applications. We are currently at an early stage of deploying
L3/L4autonomousdrivingsolutionsandarecontinuingtoadvancetowardhigherlevelsofautonomy.
Weoffertwosolutions:(i)thedeploymentofoursolutionsinmass-producedvehicles(“Solutionsfor
Mass-produced Vehicles”) and (ii) the development of a scalable, driverless AD mobility and logistics
business (“Solutions for Robotaxi Services”), with potential expansion into Robovan and Robotruck
services. During the Track Record Period, revenue from Solutions for Robotaxi Services was immaterial
relative to our total revenue, as such solutions remained at an early stage of monetization. L2 assisted
drivingcouldbedividedintothreecategoriesaccordingtothedegreeofautonomy:L2-ADAS,L2-Highway
NOA and L2-Urban NOA. In 2025, independent solution providers represented 28.3% and 33.4% of the
global and China markets for L2-Highway NOA and L2-Urban NOA solutions, respectively, in terms of
sales volume. Our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles mainly assisted driving focus on the Urban NOA
segment. For our market share in the L2-Urban NOA sector and broader L2-Highway and Urban NOA
sectors,see“—MarketLandscapeandCompetition.”
WhileSolutionsforMass-producedVehiclesandSolutionsforRobotaxiServicesoperateindividually,
we have designed to foster interaction between these two solutions to drive our “One Flywheel, Two-Leg”
strategy. This strategy creates a flywheel that accelerates technological evolution and supports our path
toward scalable full autonomy. According to CIC, we are the world’s first to adopt such a “dual-leg”
strategy and demonstrate its commercial viability at scale. For more information about this strategy, see
“—Our‘OneFlywheel,Two-leg’Strategy.”
OurMarketLeadership
TechnologyLeadership
Over the years, we achieved several industry-firsts that redefined the capabilities of mass-produced
solutions. In 2023, we became the first company to deploy deep-learning-based algorithms in mass-
produced passenger vehicles, according to CIC. According to the same source, we were also the first
independent driving automation solutions provider to commercialize an end-to-end autonomous driving
system in 2024. Globally, we are the first independent driving automation solutions provider to bring
reinforcement-learning-basedmodels into mass-production in 2025, accordingto CIC. These developments
reflect our data-driven approach to scalable full autonomy. Leveraging real-world driving data generated
–1–

=== PAGE 11 ===
SUMMARY
from deployments of Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles, our models improve through an integrated
learning process, which we believe enables faster progress toward scalable Level 4 autonomous driving
capabilitiescomparedwithsimulation-focusedapproaches.
CommercialLeadership
As of December 31, 2025, we had secured cumulative nominations for 170 vehicle models, including
68 models that had reached SOP, with installation volume exceeding 680,000 units, and had established
partnershipswith24leadingglobalOEMs.
Our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles are mainly focused on the Urban NOA segment. As of
December 31, 2025, the installation volume of our Urban NOA solutions in mass-produced vehicles
had exceeded 650,000 units. As of the same date, we had secured cumulative Urban NOA nominations
for 155 vehicle models, including 57 models that had reached SOP. According to CIC, we were the
first independent Urban NOA solutions provider in China to achieve the mass-production of Urban
NOA. We also ranked first among independent Urban NOA solutions providers in China across three
key metrics: (i) sales volume of vehicles equipped with Urban NOA solutions for the trailing
12 months ended February 28, 2026; (ii) number of nominations secured as of February 28, 2026; and
(iii) number of mass-produced vehicle models incorporating our Urban NOA solutions as of
February 28, 2026. In addition, according to CIC, for the trailing 12 months ended February 28, 2026,
we ranked first globally among independent providers of Urban NOA solutions in terms of Urban NOA
sales volume, with a 64.5% market share.
Based on our technology and commercial leadership, we have built a leading position in driving
automationacrossdeploymentscale,customercoverageandcommercialization.
OurOfferingsandBusinessModel
We offer two solutions: (i) Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles; and (ii) Solutions for Robotaxi
Services.
SolutionsforMass-producedVehicles
As vehicles transition from mechanical products to software-driven systems, advanced driving
automationisbecomingafoundationalelementofvehicledesign,productionandlifecyclemanagement.As
a Tier-1 software supplier, we provide OEMs with production-ready driving automation software solutions
designed for real-world stability and cross-platform adaptability, enabling OEMs to retain control over
system deployment and upgrades while accelerating time-to-market. Leveraging proven mass-production
deliverycapabilities,wearethefirstTier-1suppliertoofferfullsystem-levelsoftware,accordingtoCIC.
OEMs select us for our ability to deliver production-ready driving automation solutions at scale, with
system-level responsibility for performance, safety and deployment. As of December 31, 2025, we had
established relationship with 24 leading global OEMs, including Mercedes-Benz, BMW Group China,
Audi, Toyota, Honda and Dongfeng Nissan, with deployments across eight of the world’s top ten OEM
groups and all of China’s top ten OEM groups. As of February 28, 2026, we had further established a
relationship with Ford, bringing the number of the world’s top 10 OEMs with which we had established
relationships to nine. Our platform-agnostic Momenta Mainline supports efficient participation in global
programsandongoingcollaborationwithOEMsonL3commercialization.
During the Track Record Period, revenue generated from our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles
business consisted of (i) pre-production technical development services, where we adapt, validate and
integrate our solutions into OEMs’ vehicle models intended for mass-production; and (ii) post-production
volume-based licensing fees. Such licensing fees are charged once for each vehicle produced with our AD
solutionsintegrated.See“—OurRevenueModel—SolutionsforMass-producedVehicles.”

SolutionsforRobotaxiServices
Our Solutions for Robotaxi Services currently focus on Robotaxi services, with plans to expand into
Robovan and Robotruck as technology and commercialization mature. In our marketing and commercial
activities, we generally refer to this business as “Scalable Robo.” According to CIC, we were the first
company globally to deploy Robotaxi services using mass-produced vehicles equipped with our driving
automation solutions. Since initiating large-scale robotaxi deployment in 2020, we have obtained
commercial operating approvals in Suzhou and Shanghai, pilot operation permits and testing approvals in
Wuxi, as well as testing approvals in Abu Dhabi, where we secured a city-wide testing permit within
approximatelythreemonths,amongthefastestapprovaltimelinesintheindustry,accordingtoCIC.Weare
collaborating with Mercedes-Benz and Lumo to launch the world’s first premium robotaxi and, together
with EnjoyGo, have obtained the permits for unmanned operations in Shanghai in January 2026. We have
also established cooperation frameworks with global mobility platforms including Uber and Grab and plan
to launch international commercial robotaxi services in Abu Dhabi and Munich in 2026, followed by
expectedexpansionintoadditionalcitiesintheMiddleEast,EuropeandSoutheastAsia,suchasDubaiand
Singapore, as well as selected cities in Germany. Currently, we have completed system integration with
Uber and are conducting testing in Munich, and are engaging with Grab on regulatory approvals and
early-stagetestingarrangements,whileinAbuDhabiweareconductingnecessaryon-roadtesting.
WebelieveourSolutionsforRobotaxiServicescangrowfasterthanourpeersduetothreekeyfactors.
First, our map-free architecture allows us to quickly enter new cities, reducing costs and speeding up
deployment, while also supporting international expansion without the need for detailed maps in each new
market. Second, we collect large amounts of real-world driving data from mass-produced vehicles, which
improves our models and helps us address safety issues more effectively. Lastly, we use reinforcement
learningtocontinuouslyenhanceourmodels’decision-making,makingthemsaferthanhumandrivers.
During the Track Record Period, revenue from Solutions for Robotaxi Services was primarily derived
fromourshareofridefares,calculatedasafixedpercentagespecifiedintherelevantagreements,generated
fromrobotaxioperationsincollaborationwithmobilityplatforms.
Our“OneFlywheel,Two-leg”Strategy
We have developed a unique “One Flywheel, Two-leg” strategy that integrates Solutions for
Mass-produced Vehicle and Solutions for Robotaxi Services. The Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicle
segment involves deploying our Urban NOA-focused solutions in vehicles produced by OEM customers.
Thesevehiclescollectlargevolumesofreal-worlddata,whichimproveouralgorithmsand,inturn,support
our Solutions for Robotaxi Services. The advancements made in Robotaxi technology feed back into
SolutionsforMass-producedVehicle,creatingacontinuouscycleofimprovementinbothsegments.
This strategy is commercially and technologically distinct because it combines Solutions for
Mass-produced Vehicle technology and Solutions for Robotaxi Services on the same platform, whereas
competitors typically focus on only one of these areas. Commercially, this approach is unique, as our
large-scale deployment of Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles provide a stable revenue stream, allowing us
to advance cutting-edge Robotaxi technologies and secure long-term growth. Technologically, our model is
differentiatedbytheintegrationofadvancedtechnologies,suchastheR6ReinforcementLearningLargeModel
(R6Model).Unliketraditionalmodels,theR6Modelcontinuouslyimprovesbyreinforcingoptimalbehaviors,
resultinginbettersafety,compliance,anddrivingintelligence.Italsobenefitsfromtheextensivedatacollected
bymass-producedvehicles—anadvantagethatcompetitorsrelyingsolelyonRobotaxioperationsareunableto
leverage. Combined with innovations like map-free technology, our approach provides a faster, more scalable
pathtocommercializingSolutionsforRobotaxiServicescomparedtotraditionalmethods.

INNOVATIVECOMPANY
We believe we satisfy the suitability requirement of being an innovative company as defined in
paragraph4of Chapter2.2 of theGuide.Ourabilitytosatisfythisrequirementisprimarilyunderpinnedby
our “One Flywheel, Two-leg” business model innovation. This business model integrates our Solutions for
Mass-producedVehiclesbusinessandourSolutionsforRobotaxiServiceswithinaunifiedcommercialand
technologicalframework.AccordingtoCIC,wepioneeredthe“OneFlywheel,Two-leg”businessmodelin
theintelligentdrivingsolutionsindustry.
This business model is commercially differentiated from other industry participants because it
combines mass-production deployment and staged monetization with the development of higher-level
autonomousdrivingapplicationswithinoneoperatingframework,ratherthanfocusingononlyoneofthese
areas. Under this model, our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles business provides current
commercialization, OEM program integration and large-scale real-world driving data, while our Solutions
for Robotaxi Services provides additionaloperational and validationscenarios for higher-level autonomous
driving applications. The two business legs are designed to reinforce each other in both commercialization
andtechnologydevelopment.
This business model is also technologically differentiated because both business legs operate on a
shared technology foundation and allow reuse of relevant data, algorithms, toolchains and validation
capabilities across different application scenarios. In particular, our driving datasets and algorithm
development benefit from multiple data collection scenarios, including mass-produced vehicles equipped
with our solutions, our own testing fleet and our L4 operations. Our larger mass-production deployment
enables us to obtain substantial volumes of real-world driving data on a continuous basis, including low-
frequency and long-tail driving events that are difficult to obtain without broad fleet exposure. In addition,
we have developed standardized internal methods to categorize uploaded driving data by specific driving
situations, assign predefined quality labels to data segments, and convert raw driving data into training-
ready datasets. As a result, we are able to identify and extract more high-value driving data and iterate and
validateour algorithmsacross a broader range of real-world driving conditionsthanindependentintelligent
drivingsolutionsprovidersoperatingatasmallerdeploymentscale.
For further details, see “Business—Our Strengths—Our Software Tier-1 Business Model, Supported
by Mainline Platform Delivery Capabilities,” “Business—Our Solutions—Our Revenue Model,”
“Business—Our Technologies—Our Flywheel Approach,” “Business—Our Technologies—The R6 Model
andItsKeyEnhancements,”andrelatedsections.

WVRSTRUCTURE
Our Company has adopted the WVR structure, effective upon Listing, to enable the WVR
Beneficiaries to exercise voting control over our Company. Under our WVR structure, our share capital
comprisesClassA OrdinaryShares andClassBOrdinaryShares.EachClassAOrdinaryShareentitlesthe
holder to exercise one vote, and each Class B Ordinary Share entitles the holder to exercise ten votes,
respectively,onmatterssubjecttovotingatgeneralmeetingsofourCompany,subjecttoRule8A.24ofthe
Listing Rules that requires the Reserved Matters to be voted on a one-vote-per-share basis. For further
details relating to (i) the weighted voting rights attached to Class B Ordinary Shares, (ii) the WVR
Beneficiaries and (iii) the beneficial interests held by, and voting rights controlled by, the WVR
Beneficiaries, see “Share Capital” in this prospectus. For further information about the rights, preferences,
–5–

SUMMARY
privileges and restrictions of the Class A Ordinary Shares and Class B Ordinary Shares, see “Summary of
the Constitution of Our Company and the Company Laws of the Cayman Islands — 2 Articles of
Association”inAppendixIIItothisprospectus.
Prospective investors are advised to be aware of the potential risks of investing in companies with
weighted voting rights structures, in particular that interests of the WVR Beneficiaries may not necessarily
always be aligned with those of our Shareholders as a whole, and that the WVR Beneficiaries will be in a
position to exercise their higher voting power to influence the affairs of our Company and the outcome of
Shareholders’ resolutions, irrespective of how other Shareholders vote. Prospective investors should make
the decision to invest in our Company only after due and careful consideration. For further information
about the risks associated with the WVR structure adopted by the Company, see “Risk Factors — Risks
RelatedtotheWVRStructure”inthisprospectus.

Non-IFRSMeasures
Weuseadjustedlossfortheyear(non-IFRSmeasure),whichisanon-IFRSmeasure,inevaluatingour
operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. We believe that adjusted loss
for the year (non-IFRS measure) provides useful information about our results of operations, enhances the
overallunderstandingofourpastperformanceandfutureprospects.
Adjustedlossfortheyear(non-IFRSmeasure)shouldnotbeconsideredinisolationorconstruedasan
alternative to loss for the year. Adjusted loss for the year (non-IFRS measure) presented here may not be
comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate
similarlytitledmeasuresdifferently,limitingtheirusefulnessascomparativemeasurestoourdata.
We define our adjusted loss for the year (non-IFRS measure) by adding back (i) share-based
compensation expense, (ii) changes in fair value of Preferred Shares and other financial liabilities, and
(iii)listingexpenses, to loss for the year. We excludethese itemsbecausetheyarenotexpectedtoresultin
future cash payments or relate to this Global Offering. Specifically, (i) share-based compensation expense
relates to the share-based awards that we grant to participants of our share incentive schemes is a non-cash
expense, (ii) changes in fair value of Preferred Shares and other financial liabilities are non-cash in nature,
and Preferred Shares and other financial liabilities will be converted into the equity of our Company upon
thecompletionoftheGlobalOffering,and(iii)listingexpensesrelatestothisGlobalOffering.

MARKETLANDSCAPEANDCOMPETITION
The market for L2-Highway NOA, L2-Urban NOA assisted driving and higher-level driving
automation solutions is highly competitive and growing rapidly, reaching approximately US$16.5 billion
globally and US$10.4 billion in China in 2025, and expected to increase to approximately US$70.3 billion
and US$38.6 billion, respectively, 2030. Within the Urban NOA segment, we have established a leading
position in China. Additionally, autonomous driving based on dedicated fleets is emerging across
applications such as robotaxis, robovans and robotrucks. Although the robotaxi market remained
US$0.1 billion globally and in China in 2025, it is projected to reach approximately US$81.8 billion
globally and US$38.1 billion in China by 2030, with penetration expected to rise to 5.7% globally and
11.9% in China. In terms of sales volume for the 12 months ended February in 2026, we achieved market
shares of 64.5% in the Urban NOA sector and 27.4% in the broader Highway and Urban NOA sector. For
details,see“IndustryOverview.”
RISKFACTORS
Our business and the Global Offering involve significant risks as described in “Risk Factors” in this
Prospectus,whichshouldbereadcarefullyinitsentiretybeforemakinganinvestmentdecision.Majorrisks
include: (i) autonomous driving remains an emerging and rapidly evolving industry characterized by
technological uncertainty, limited operating history and evolving regulatory requirements, making our
future performance difficult to predict; (ii) the markets for driving automation solutions and our Solutions
for Robotaxi Services are still developing, and commercialization may not progress as expected; (iii) our
growth depends on securing and maintaining relationships with major OEM customers, obtaining and
retaining development program nominations, and successfully converting such nominations into mass-
production revenue, which may involve delays, volume uncertainty or contract termination risks; (iv) our
solutionsrelyoncomplexalgorithmsandsoftwaresystemsthatmaycontaindefectsor performanceissues,
potentially leading to safety concerns, liability exposure or reputational harm; and (v) compliance with
evolving cybersecurity, data protection and information security laws may increase costs or expose us to
regulatoryactionsthatcouldadverselyaffectourbusiness,financialconditionandresultsofoperations.

DIVIDENDS
We currently have no plan to declare or pay any dividends in the near future on our shares, as we
currently intend to retain most, if not all, of our available funds and any future earnings to operate and
expand our business. During the Track Record Period, no dividend was paid or declared by us. Currently,
we do not have a formal dividend policy or a fixed dividend payout ratio. Our Board has discretion as to
whether to distribute dividends, subject to certain requirements of Cayman Islands law. Under Cayman
Islands law, a Cayman Islands company may pay a dividend out of either profit or share premium account,
provided that in no circumstances may a dividend be paid if this would result in the company being unable
to pay its debts as they fall due in the ordinary course of business. Even if our Board decides to pay
dividends, the form, frequency and amount will depend upon our future operations and earnings, capital
requirements and surplus, general financial condition, contractual restrictions and other factors that the
Board may deem relevant. As advised by our legal advisor as to Cayman Islands law, notwithstanding that
the Company may have accumulated losses, the Company may declare dividend (a) out of profits of the
Company if the Company has sufficient profits, realized or unrealized, unless such is contrary to the
accountingprinciplesadoptedbytheCompanyor(b)outofthesharepremiumoftheCompanyiffollowing
the date on which the dividendis proposed to be paid, theCompanyisabletopayitsdebtsas theyfalldue
intheordinarycourseofbusiness.

RecentRegulatoryDevelopments
Recent media reports indicate that the PRC authorities have slowed the issuance of new autonomous
driving permits nationwide following a temporary service outage involving certain robotaxi operations. In
response,wehavemaintainedcommunicationwiththerelevantregulatoryauthoritiesandcloselymonitored
the latest regulatory requirements, review standards and permit application procedures applicable to
autonomous driving testing, demonstration application and demonstration operation. During the Track
Record Period and as of the Latest Practicable Date, we had not identified any material adverse actual or
expected impact of such reported developments on our business operations, growth plans or business
prospects. In particular, we do not expect such reported developments to have a material direct impact on
our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles business, as such business principally involves the provision of
assisted driving solutions for mass-produced passenger vehicles, including L2 Highway NOA, L2 Urban
NOA and higher-level solutions for OEM customers, and does not depend on the issuance of robotaxi
testing or operation permits. Accordingly, the reported tightening of new autonomous driving permits for
robotaxi operations does not directly affect our existing mass-production programs. In addition, given that
our Solutions for Robotaxi Services represented an immaterial portion of our revenue during the Track
Record Period and that we continued to make steady progress in overseas markets, we do not expect such
reported developments to have a material adverse effect on our revenue, costs, results of operations or
financial condition. We will continue to monitor relevant regulatory developments and maintain
communication with the relevant regulatory authorities regarding applicable regulatory requirements and
approval procedures. As of the Latest Practicable Date, our existing testing and operational permits,
includingthoserelatingtoourSolutionsforRobotaxiServices,inthePRCallremainedvalidandeffective,
andhadnotbeensuspended,revokedorotherwisesubjecttoregulatoryrestrictions.Asofthesamedate,we
had not experienced any material delay, suspension or other material adverse impact in respect of our L4
business expansion plans or the application for, renewal of or maintenance of relevant testing,
demonstration application or demonstration operation permits. For details, see “Business — Licenses,
Permits and Approvals” and “Regulatory Overview — Regulations Related to Driving Automation and
IntelligentConnectedVehicles.”

exposureandcontrollabilityofpotentialhazards

AsusedinthisProspectus,unlessotherwiseindicated:
• the “number of SOPs” refers to the number of mass-produced vehicle models that are equipped
with our solutions; we consider cumulative number of SOPs achieved to be a key performance
measure because SOP represents a crucial milestone in our relationships with OEMs, signaling
the commencement of mass-production for a new vehicle model and enabling us to generate
additionalrevenuestreams,includinglicensingfees;
• we track and use the “number of OEMs” with whom we have established relationships as key
performance metrics to evaluate our business and growth strategies because our current customer
base consists mainly of OEMs and we have been focused on building and expanding our
relationshipswithOEMs;
• a “nomination” refers to the event that an OEM selects a supplier’s solution for integration into
thedesignanddevelopmentofanewvehiclemodel;post-nomination,thesupplier’ssolutionwill
undergo extensive testing and validation, often spanning several years, to meet the OEM’s
stringent standards; this process culminates at the SOP stage, where the solution is officially
incorporatedintotheOEM’smass-producedvehicles.Asupplierachievinganominationtypically
receives a “letter of nomination” from the OEM reflecting the OEM’s intention to form a formal
cooperative relationship and is issued to companies deemed qualified suppliers for certain
solutions. Usually, the OEM selects a single supplier for each specific requirement, such as an
driving automationsolution for a designated vehicle model. However, these lettersof nomination
are not legally binding and do not guarantee that the supplier’s solution will ultimately be
incorporated into the OEM’s mass-produced vehicle models. We consider cumulative number of
nominations to be a key performance measure to evaluate our business because it indicates our
ability to convert OEMs into our customers and secure new projects with OEMs who are our
existing customers. In this Prospectus, the cumulative number of nominations as of a given
dateincludesnominationsforvehiclemodelsthathavereachedSOPasofthesamedate;
• the term “having established relationships” with an OEM means that we have obtained a
nomination from that OEM and/or signed legally binding contracts with that OEM directly or
indirectly through its designated tier-1 supplier(s); We are considered to have “established
relationships”withanOEMif,duringtherelevantperiod,we(i)obtainedanominationfromsuch
OEM, (ii) generated revenue from such OEM, or (iii) were engaged in an ongoing technical
developmentservicesprojectwithsuchOEM.

RISKSRELATEDTOOURBUSINESSANDINDUSTRY
AD technology is an emerging technology and involves significant risks and uncertainties. Our limited
operating history makes it difficult to evaluate our prospects and the risks and challenges we may
encounterinthefuture.
Despite technological advancements and the commercialization success by some companies, driving
automationsolutionsmarketisstillfacedwithasignificantnumberoftechnicalandcommercialchallenges,
including an expectation for better-than-human driving performance, significant investment demands,
extended timelines for vehicle development, the specialized nature of the workforce, changing regulatory
environments, a need to build public trust and brand image, and the practical application of emerging
technologies. If we fail to navigate these challenges successfully, our business, prospects, financial
condition,andresultsofoperationswillbenegativelyimpacted.
Wecommencedoperationsin2016andbegancommercialdeploymentofoursolutionsin2019.Given
ourrelativelylimitedoperatinghistoryinarapidlyevolvingindustry,ourlong-termprospectsandabilityto
forecast future operating results remain subject to significant uncertainty. Our future performance will

OnAugust9,2023,theBidenadministrationpublishedanexecutiveorder,andtheTreasurypublishedan
advanced notice of proposed rulemaking (the “ANPRM”) providing a conceptual framework for outbound
investment controls focused on China, including Hong Kong and Macau (the “Outbound Investment
Program” or the “OIP”). Further to this ANPRM, on June 21, 2024, Treasury issued a proposed rule on
outboundU.S. investments involvingChinathatis generallyconsistentinits requirements withtheANPRM.
On October 28, 2024, Treasury issued a Final Rule to implement the executive order of August 9, 2023. The
Final Rule took effect on January 2, 2025. The Final Rule targets investments involving persons and entities
associatedwith“countriesofconcern,”currentlyChina,includingtheSARregionsofHongKongandMacau.
The OIP imposes investment prohibitions and notification requirements on U.S. persons (which are broadly
definedundertheFinalRule,including,amongothers,U.S.-incorporatedentities,U.S.citizensandpermanent
residents wherever located, branches of U.S. entities outside the United States, and any person in the United
States) in a range of investments in companies engaged in, or having significant financial ties to companies
engaged in, certain activities relating to three technology sectors: (i) semiconductors and microelectronics,
(ii) quantum information technologies, and (iii) artificial intelligence systems. Under the OIP, “Covered
Foreign Persons” include, but are not limited to, (i) companies that are engaged in one of these three
technology sectors and that are headquartered, incorporated in, or have their principal place of business in a
“country of concern,” (ii) companies that are engaged in one of these three technology sectors and that are
directly or indirectly ownedbythegovernmentof a“countryof concern”or bycertainindividuals or entities
associated with a “country of concern,” and (iii) companies with significant financial ties to companies
described in (i) or (ii). Investments by U.S. persons subject to the OIP, which are defined as “covered
transactions,”includecertaintransactionsinvolving“CoveredForeignPersons,”includingcertainacquisitions
of equity interests andcontingentequityinterests, debtfinancing, jointventures, andinvestments as alimited
partnerinanon-U.S.personpooledinvestmentfund.TheOIPrequiresparentU.S.person-entitiesofnon-U.S.
entities to “take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent any transaction by” their non-U.S. entities that
would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person. The OIP’s notification requirements also
applytoU.S.person-entitiesthataretheparentsofnon-U.S.entitiesthatenterintotransactionsthatwouldbe
notifiabletransactionsifenteredintobyaU.S.person.
The OIP prohibits U.S. persons from knowingly directing a non-U.S. person from entering into a
transaction that would be prohibited if entered into by a U.S. person. The OIP includes some exceptions

Under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and its implementation rules, an enterprise established
outside of the PRC with a “de facto management body” within the PRC is considered a PRC resident
enterprise.Theimplementationrulesdefinetheterm“defactomanagementbody”asthebodythatexercises
full and substantial control over and overall management of the business, productions, personnel, accounts
and properties of an enterprise. In 2009, the State Taxation Administration, or the STA, issued a circular,
known as Circular 82, which provides certain specific criteria for determining whether the “de facto
management body” of a PRC-controlled enterprise that is incorporated offshore is located in China.
Although Circular 82 only applies to offshore enterprises controlled by PRC enterprises or PRC enterprise
groups, not those controlled by PRC individuals or foreigners like us, the criteria set forth in the circular
may reflect the State Taxation Administration’s general position on how the “de facto management body”
test should be applied in determining the tax resident status of all offshore enterprises. According to
Circular 82, an offshore incorporated enterprise controlled by a PRC enterprise or a PRC enterprise group
will be regarded as a PRC tax resident by virtue of having its “de facto management body” in China and
willbesubjecttoPRCenterpriseincometaxonitsglobalincomeonlyifallofthefollowingconditionsare
met:(i)theprimarylocationoftheday-to-dayoperationalmanagementisinthePRC;(ii)decisionsrelating
to the enterprise’s financial and human resource matters are made or are subject to approval by
organizations or personnel in the PRC; (iii) the enterprise’s primary assets, accounting books and records,
company seals, and board and shareholder resolutions, are located or maintained in the PRC; and (iv) at
least50%ofvotingboardmembersorseniorexecutiveshabituallyresideinthePRC.
We believe that none of our entities outside of China is a PRC resident enterprise for PRC tax
purposes. However, the tax resident status of an enterprise is subject to determination by the PRC tax
authorities, and the interpretation of the term “de facto management body” may be evolving and subject to
change. If the PRC tax authorities determine that we, or any of our subsidiaries incorporated outside of the
PRC,areaPRCresidententerpriseforenterpriseincometaxpurposes,weorsuchsubsidiarywillbesubject

Our shareholders may face difficulties in protecting their interests, and the ability to protect their rights
throughHongKongcourtsmaybelimitedbecauseweareincorporatedunderCaymanIslandslaw.
We are an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands. Our corporate
affairs are governed by our Memorandum and Articles, the Companies Act (as amended) of the
Cayman Islands and the common law of the Cayman Islands. The rights of shareholders to take action
against our directors, actions by our minority shareholders and the fiduciary duties of our directors to
us under Cayman Islands law are to a large extent governed by the common law of the Cayman Islands.
The common law of the Cayman Islands is derived in part from comparatively limited judicial
precedent in the Cayman Islands as well as from the common law of England and Wales, the decisions
of whose courts are of persuasive authority, but are not binding, on a court in the Cayman Islands. As a
result, the rights of our shareholders and the fiduciary duties of our directors under Cayman Islands law
may not be as clearly established as they would be under the laws of some other jurisdictions,
including Hong Kong. In particular, the Cayman Islands have a less developed body of securities laws
than Hong Kong.
The Cayman Islands law and practice relating to shareholder actions (including the ability to bring
derivative actions), shareholder remedies and the enforcement of directors’ duties may differ from
those in Hong Kong, and such differences may make it more difficult for shareholders to protect their
interests. In addition, Cayman Islands companies may not have the standing to initiate a shareholder
derivative action in in certain jurisdictions, and shareholders may face additional hurdles in pursuing
litigation or obtaining remedies outside the Cayman Islands. Moreover, while in some jurisdictions
controlling shareholders may owe fiduciary duties to the companies they control and/or minority
shareholders, under Cayman Islands law, controlling shareholders generally do not owe fiduciary
duties to the company or minority shareholders merely by virtue of their shareholding. Accordingly,
our controlling shareholders may exercise their powers as shareholders, including the exercise of
voting rights in respect of their shares, in such manner as they think fit.
Shareholders of Cayman Islands exempted companies like us have no general rights under Cayman
Islands law to inspect corporate records (other than the Memorandum and Articles, the register of
mortgages and charges and any special resolutions passed by shareholders) or to obtain copies of lists of
shareholders of thesecompanies.TotheextentpermissibleundertheArticleswhichshallbeincompliance
with the Listing Rules, our directors have discretion under our articles of association to determine the
closureoftheregisterofmembers.Thismaymakeitmoredifficultforyoutoobtaintheinformationneeded
to establish any facts necessary for a shareholder motion or to solicit proxies from other shareholders in
connectionwithaproxycontest.
Certain corporate governance practices in the Cayman Islands, which is our home country, differ
significantly from requirements for companies incorporated in other jurisdictions such as Hong Kong. To
the extent we are permitted to, and do, follow home country practices, our shareholders may be afforded
less protectionthan they otherwise would under rules and regulationsapplicabletocompaniesincorporated
inHongKong.

OVERVIEWOFDRIVINGAUTOMATION
Driving automation has quickly moved from a niche technology to a mainstream feature of modern
vehicles. What once appeared only in high-end models as optional driver-assistance functions to enhance
safety and comfort isnow becomingstandardacross awiderrangeof mass-marketvehicles. Currently,due
to regulatory constraints, the large-scale deployment of this technology remains limited to L2 stage.
However, given differing technical difficulty and implemented functions, the L2 segment can be further
dividedintothreecategories:L2-ADAS,L2-HighwayNOA,andL2-UrbanNOA.
From a functional perspective, L2-ADAS solutions generally operate as individual, driver-invoked
assistancefeatures.Bycontrast,L2-UrbanNOA andL2-HighwayNOA solutionsaredesignedtosupporta
continuous, route-based assisted driving experience, in which the system can perform a sequence of
maneuvers such as steering, accelerationand deceleration,lanechanges, overtakingandobstacleavoidance
without requiring the driver to re-trigger each maneuver separately. At present, L2-Urban NOA systems
represent the most advanced and commercially viable segments, driven by the rapid rollout of NOA
functionsinurbanscenarios.
According to the degreeof automation,therearebroadlytwocategorieswithinthedrivingautomation
market. The first category is L1 and L2-ADAS, which is also known as advanced driver assistance
–92–

=== PAGE 102 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
systems (“ADAS”). These systems assist the driver with specific driving tasks with common ADAS
functionsincludingadaptivecruisecontrol,lanekeepingandassistanceinstop-and-gotraffic.
The second category is L2-Highway NOA, L2-Urban NOA assisted driving and higher-level driving
automation.ComparedwithADAS,thesesystemsaredesignedtotakeonabroadersetofdrivingtasksand
operatewithahigherdegreeofautonomyandundermorecomplexroadconditions.
The rapid adoption of L2-Highway NOA, L2-Urban NOA assisted driving and higher-level driving
automation technologies is driving a fundamental shift in driving automation, similar to the transition from
feature phones to smartphones in the mobile industry. With traditional ADAS reaching broad maturity, the
commercializationof these technologies, particularly Urban NOA, marked a clear industry turning point in
2024, delivering a meaningful improvement in real-world driving experience. This shift accelerated the
transition from basic driver assistance toward higher levels of automation and moved large-scale
autonomousmobilitymateriallyclosertopracticaldeployment.Asaresult,OEMsareincreasinglyviewing
driving automation not as a feature upgrade, but as a core pillar of vehicle differentiation, user experience
andlong-termproductstrategy.

Two Business Models in Autonomous Driving: Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles and Solutions for
RobotaxiServices
The commercialization of L2-Highway NOA, L2-Urban NOA and higher-level technologies broadly
follows two primary business models: a mass-production model and a scalable robo model. While both are
ultimately aimed at achieving full autonomy, they differ fundamentally in how autonomy is developed,
deployedandmonetized.
Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles: Under Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles, driving
automationtechnologiesaredeployedonmass-producedvehicleswithcommercializationprimarilydrivenby
a project-based development fee for initial customization, integration, and validation of such technology. As
vehicle model enters mass-productions and gradually scales, commercialization can pivot diverse fee models
suchaslicense,subscription,andhardwaresalesformoreextensivemonetizationopportunities.Furthermore,
vehicles equipped with these solutions operate in everyday traffic and continuously generate real-world
drivingdata,includingrareandcomplexcornercases.Asmorevehiclesequippedwithsuchsolutionsaresold,
the quantity and diversity of driving data expand accordingly, creating a closed loop of data accumulation,
algorithmimprovementandproductrefinement.Atpresent,UrbanNOArepresentsthemostadvancedlevelof
vehicleautomationthathasbeenbroadlycommercializedonmass-producedvehicles.
–93–

=== PAGE 103 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Thismodelhasseveraldefiningcharacteristics:
• Extensive vehicle scale to accumulate corner cases at lower cost. By relying on mass-produced
vehiclesforconsumersratherthandedicatedfleets,themass-productionmodelenablesdatacollection
acrossvastgeographiesandoperatingconditionsatasubstantiallylowermarginalcostpervehicle.This
allowsrareandcomplexdrivingsituationstobediscoveredandcollectedmoreefficientlyatscale.
• Rapidalgorithmiterationtoenablesmarterdrivingautomationsystem.Continuousexposure
to diverse driving conditions, particularly high-value corner cases, allows driving automation
systems to be trained and iterated at a rapid pace. Over time, this drives more natural, stable and
human-likedrivingbehavioracrossanexpandingrangeofscenarios.
• Extensivevalidationofscalablesafety.Thegrowingvolumeofreal-worldoperatingdataallows
safetyperformancetobewidelytested,refinedandvalidatedacrossbillionsofdrivingmiles.This
supports continuous improvements in perception and planning accuracy, decision-making speed
andvehiclecontrol,andcontributestosteadilyloweraccidentriskasthesystemmatures.
• Strengthened generalization capability enabling broader deployment. Solutions for
Mass-produced Vehicles enables L2-Highway NOA, L2-Urban NOA and higher-level
technologies to scale across diverse vehicle models and regions, leading to broader deployment.
Proventhroughextensivemass-productionexperience,suchtechnologycanbequicklyadaptedto
different OEM platforms, requirements, and specific hardware configurations. Meanwhile,
large-scaled validation across roads, cities, and vehicle platforms, coupled with the map-free
technology, can significantly enhance system generalization capabilities and shorten time to
deployinnewscenarios.
• A financially sustainable path to autonomy. Each additional mass-produced vehicle not only
generates valuable new data, validates safety and boosts generalization, but also contributes recurring
revenue and cash flow that can be reinvested into research and development. This creates a
commercially sustainable loop that supports long-term technological advancement toward full
autonomy.Thisfinancialstructureisparticularlyimportantastheindustrymovestowardfullautonomy,
whereresearchanddevelopmentactivitiesarelong-term,continuousandhighlycapital-intensive.
Solutions for Robo: This model advances autonomy through the deployment of dedicated fleets, such
as Robotaxi, Robovan, and Robotruck. Unlike mass-production model, these vehicles are operated as
centralized fleets rather than sold to individual consumers. Commercial rollout under this model typically
begins only after obtaining regulatory approvals from pilot cities and is restricted to pre-defined operating
zones. Vehicles run on controlled routes and under defined operating conditions, and revenue is generated
directlyfrommobilityorlogisticsservices,aswellas,insomecases,vehiclesales.
This model offers a direct path to fully driverless operation within confined domains, but it also
requires substantial upfront capital investment, extended regulatory lead times and ongoing fleet-level
operating and maintenance infrastructure. As a result, expansion tends to follow a city-by-city,
route-by-routeprocess,andscalingisgenerallymoregradualandcostly.

L2-HighwayNOA/L2-UrbanNOAandHigher-levelSolutionIsBecomingthePrimaryValueDriverof
VehicleAutomation
The progress of deploying L2-Highway NOA / L2-Urban NOA and higher-level technology on mass-
produced vehicles is being supported by two parallel developments: continued improvements in hardware,
such as sensors and computing platforms, and rapid advancement in such solution, where the algorithmic
stack defines how effectively the hardware is utilized and ultimately determines real-world driving
performance. While stronger hardware provides the physical foundation for automation, it is the driving
automation solution that turns raw sensing and computing capability into practical, user-facing driving
functions.
As vehicles become more automated, the economic and functional center of gravity is shifting from
hardware to software. Driving automation solution defines how accurately a vehicle understands its
surroundings, how well it anticipates traffic behavior, and how it makes driving decisions in complex real-
worldconditions.Inpractice,thissolutionsetstheupperlimitofwhatavehiclecandoautonomously.
Unlike hardware, which is largely fixed once installed, driving automation solution can be
continuouslyupgradedthroughover-the-airupdates.Thisallowsvehiclefunctionalitytoimproveovertime
without replacingphysical components, extends the effectivelife of thevehicleplatform,andkeepssystem
performancecurrent as algorithmsevolve. At the same time, increasinglydemandingsolution requirements
are shaping the design of future hardware platforms, raising the bar for system integration, computing
redundancy and sensing reliability. In this sense, driving automation solution is no longer just consuming
hardwarecapabilitybutisalsoincreasinglydrivinghardwarearchitecturedecisions.
Astheroleofdrivingautomationsolutionbecomesmorecentral,theindustry’scommercialmodelsare
also evolving in ways that support long-term, recurring growth. Today, driving automation solutions
providers typically generate revenue through a combination of non-recurring engineering fees paid by
OEMs for each vehicle platform and per-vehicle license fees tied to production volumes. As more vehicle
models adopt the same underlying software capabilities, license revenue becomes an increasingly
significantandscalabledriveroflong-termincome.
Looking ahead, as consumers place greater value on driving automation functionality, the industry is
expected to move further toward subscription-based fee models, under which vehicle owners pay recurring
–98–

=== PAGE 108 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
fees for advanced driving features and continuous software upgrades. This structure offers stronger
alignment between OEMs and driving automation solutions providers, enhances revenue visibility and
createsamoredurableandprofitablegrowthprofileoverthevehiclelifecycle.
GrowthDriversfortheL2-HighwayNOA/L2-UrbanNOAandHigher-levelSolutionsMarket
Market Demand: Rising consumer demands accelerates OEM adoption of driving automation
solutions. From a consumer-demand perspective, Urban NOA and Highway NOA are increasingly viewed
as a must-have feature rather than a nice-to-have add-on. This directly increases willingness to pay and
makesthesefeatureskeypurchasedifferentiator.Demandisdrivenbytwoclearvaluepropositions.Firstis
convenience. Urban NOA and Highway NOA meaningfully reduce repetitive and time-consuming driving
tasks, which is especially valued in cities where the average commute exceeds one hour. Second is safety.
Consumers are placing greater weight on proven safety outcomes. According to CIC, L2-Highway NOA /
L2-Urban NOA and higher-leveltechnologycan achievearound a 70% reductionin crash rates with multi-
sensor perception and real-time decision-making capabilities beyond human limitations. As these benefits
become more visible, consumer pull accelerates and pushes OEMs to roll out Urban NOA and Highway
NOAfeaturesacrossbroadermodelstostaycompetitiveandcaptureincrementaldemand.
Market Supply: Technological breakthroughs enhance driving automation performance. Advances
in core algorithmsare steadilyimprovingnot only the performanceof drivingautomationsystems, butalso
their economic feasibility at scale. As models evolve from deep learning and transform towards more
advanced machine learning approach such as reinforcement-learning, driving automation systems are
becomingbetterathandlingcomplexinteractionsindenseurbantraffic.Theseimprovementsarehelpingto
resolvelong-standingcorner-casechallengesinUrbanNOA,shorteningdevelopmentcyclesandsupporting
widercommercialdeployment.
Policiestailwindtostimulatefuturedevelopment.Policysupportisalsoplayinganincreasinglyimportant
role in the next phase of market development, with China at the forefront of market-enabling regulation. In
September 2025, China’s MIITandsevenotheragenciesissuedtheAutomobileIndustrySteadyGrowthWork
Plan(2025-2026),whichconditionallyallowsLevel3vehiclesandestablishessupportingframeworksforroad
safety, liability allocation and insurance. The policy helps address key barriers to L3 commercialization by
clarifying liability and insurance arrangements, areas that have historically constrained large-scale deployment
despite technological readiness. In December 2025, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
conditionallyapprovedChina’sfirstbatchofLevel3autonomousdrivingvehiclemodelsforpilotroadoperation
indesignatedareasofBeijingandChongqing,markinganimportantstepfromtestinganddemonstrationtoward
regulated commercialization of L3 functions, marking the transition of L3 vehicles from testing and
demonstration toward regulated road operation, creating a pathway for broader commercial deployment and
future scale-up. At the local level, governments are also accelerating implementation. Beijing’s Autonomous
DrivingVehicleOrdinancetookeffectonApril1,2025andisamongthemostconcretelocalpoliciessupporting
the industry, as it provides a clearer legal framework for autonomous driving technology innovation, road
application pilots, operational responsibilities and safety management. In Beijing, Level 3 vehicles have also
beengranteddefinedroadrightswithindesignateddemonstrationareas,furthersupportingthepracticalrolloutof
higher-level autonomous driving. This provided an important regulatory foundation for expanding real-world
deployment of L3 vehicles and future L4 autonomous mobility services. Meanwhile, policy tailwinds are also
building in major overseas markets. For instance, the European Union’s revised General Safety Regulation
furtherstrengthenstheregulatoryfoundationforautomatedandconnectedvehiclesbyraisingmandatorysafety
baselines and clarifying approval expectations, thereby reducing compliance uncertainty and creating a clearer
runway for broader deployment and continuous iteration of more advanced driving automation functions. The
clearer regulatory framework facilitates broader deployment of advanced driving automation functions across
Europe and supports scaling beyond pilot programs. Similarly, intheUAE, theRoads andTransportAuthority
has introduced executive regulations that set clear approval and safety requirements for vehicles equipped with
driving automation functions, including manufacturer certification. By establishing approval, certification and
operational requirements, the regulations create a clearer pathway for commercial deployment of autonomous
mobilityservicessuchasrobotaxioperations.

MarketTrendsforL2-HighwayNOA/L2-UrbanNOAandHigher-levelSolutionsMarket
Prevalence of Urban NOA technology across all vehicles price segments. Before 2024, Urban NOA
was largely confined to premium vehicle models. As algorithm efficiency has improved, however, high-

premiumfeaturetowardamainstreamproductattributeacrossmultiplepricesegments.
Overseas expansion with Chinese OEMs. China is emerging as a global leader in driving automation
market, positioning its L2-Highway NOA / L2-Urban NOA assisted driving and higher-level driving
automation solutions providers for international growth alongside OEM globalization. Rising NEV
competitiveness, improved supply-chain integration, and growing acceptance of Chinese vehicles abroad
are accelerating this expansion through partnerships with OEMs scaling overseas. As part of this process,

Germany, United Kingdom, Thailand and the UAE, while preparing for localized production and

Increasing recognition from global OEMs. Leading global OEMs are integrating Chinese driving
automation solutions into their global programs. These collaborations cover highway and urban NOA
features, as well as pilot Level 3 initiatives across Europe, Southeast Asia, and other emerging markets.
This endorsement stems from the world-leading product performance, vast data volumes, and highly
responsive service offered by Chinese providers — a combination that is solidifying their shift from
domesticsupplierstoglobaltechnologyleaders.
Independent solution providers are gaining share over fully in-house development. As competitive
pressure intensifies, OEMs are increasingly expected to offer a broad range of driving automation
capabilitiesacrossmultiplevehiclesegmentsandpricepoints.Developingandmaintainingthisfullrangeof
capabilities entirely in-house is becoming more difficult to scale efficiently in terms of cost, engineering
depth and development speed. Independent solution providers benefit from being able to serve multiple
OEM platforms at the same time. This allows them to accumulate more diverse driving data, iterate
softwaremorerapidlyandspreaddevelopmentcostsacrossalargerinstalledbase.Asaresult,manyOEMs
are shifting toward a hybrid or outsourcing model in which independent providers supply core driving
automation solutions while OEMs focus on vehicle electronic and electric design, manufacture and
integration, product positioning and branding. According to CIC, by sales volume, independent
L2-HighwayNOA/L2-UrbanNOAassisteddrivingandhigher-leveldrivingautomationsolutionproviders
accounted for 28.3% and 33.4% of the global and China markets, respectively, in 2025, representing
approximately 2.3 million units in each market, up from less than 10% globally and approximately 14% in
China in 2022. By 2030, these shares are expectedtoincreasetoaround74.9% globallyandapproximately
71.2%inChina,correspondingtosalesvolumesofapproximately30.2millionunitsand19.5millionunits,
respectively.

According to CIC, L2-Urban NOA solutions, together with L2-Highway NOA and conventional ADAS

integration, and are therefore typically priced at a materially higher level than basic, less sophisticated

for 70.6%, 18.1% and 11.3%, respectively, of the global L2 assisted driving solutions market in terms of sales

Key Success Factors for Mass-produced L2-Highway NOA / L2-Urban NOA and Higher-level Driving
AutomationSolutionsMarket
• Early-mover with extensive mass-production experience. Companies that entered
mass-production earlier benefit from a powerful accumulation effect. Large fleets of production
vehicles generate vast volumes of real-world driving data, including rare and complex situations
that are difficult to reproduce through testing alone. This data advantage directly strengthens
systemperformanceandsafetyovertime,creatingagapthatlateentrantsfindhardtoclose.
• Strong technology capabilities to craft competitive solution offerings. Leading players have
developed reinforcement-learning-based driving algorithms that enable continuous performance
improvement and robust handling of rare and complex corner cases that few competitors can
effectively address. By learning from outcomes across diverse traffic scenes, these systems can
deliver a level of safety and consistency that approaches, and in certain aspects exceeds, that of
experiencedhumandrivers,whilecontinuingtoimprovethroughongoingupdates.
• Diversified solutions to adapt varied OEM demands. As OEMs increasingly treat driving
automation technologies as core product features, they expect solution providers to offer a full
product range, from Highway NOA to Urban NOA, adaptable across multiple vehicle segments
and price points. Solutions must also integrate reliably across different vehicle platforms and
centralizedcomputingarchitectures.
• Streamlined delivery and fast time-to-market. As competition intensifies and OEM
compressing their new model launch schedules, speed of deployment is no longer optional.
Leading driving automation solutions providers with standardized software modules and
streamlined workflows are better positioned to deliver on tight OEM timelines and to support
large-scalerolloutswithoutdisruption.
• Cost efficiency and competitive pricing. Leading industry players, leveraging their experience
across a broad range of vehicle models, can reuse core hardware configurations and software
components across multiple programs. This allows them to spread development and validation
costsoveralargerproductionbase,resultinginlowerunitcostsandmorecompetitivepricingfor
OEMsseekinglarge-scaleadoption.
• Customer-oriented responsiveness. Rapid response to OEM requirements, as well as hands-on,
on-site engineering support during development and production ramp-up, has become critical
differentiators. Providers that can resolve issues quickly and work closely with OEM teams are
betterpositionedtowinprograms,meetlaunchschedulesandretainlong-termcustomers.
• Comprehensive ecosystem. Close collaboration with upstream hardware suppliers during early
design and validationstages reduces systemintegrationriskandimprovesoverallreliability.This
collaboration helps stabilize system performance, shorten development cycles and, over time,
reduce total system cost. At the same time, downstream OEMs can provide the latest market
insights, user requirements, and application scenarios that inform future solution design and
optimization.
OVERVIEWOFROBOTAXISERVICES
Scalable autonomous driving based on dedicated fleets is beginning to take shape across multiple
commercial applications including Robotaxi, Robovan, and Robotruck. Unlike the deployment of solutions
for mass-produced vehicles, this model is built around centrally operated fleets that provide transportation
orlogisticsservicesdirectlytoendusers.

Robotaxiasoneofthemostpromisingusecasesforfullautonomytoday
Amongtheseapplications,Robotaxiiswidelyviewedasthemostcommerciallyadvancedandscalable
use case for fully driverless operation in today’s market. Robotaxi services are typically deployed first in
dense urban environments, where traffic patterns are highly dynamic, road conditions vary widely and
driving routes change constantly. These conditions place the highest technical demands on autonomous
systems and generate large volumes of complex real-world driving data. This data is critical for improving
system performance, resolving corner-case behavior and accelerating the maturation of full-stack driving
automationtechnology.
From a commercial perspective, Robotaxi addresses high-frequency urban mobility demand in a
market with trillion-RMB long-term revenue potential. Urban ride-hailing is one of the largest and most
repetitivetransportationusecasesglobally,withmassivedailypassengertrafficandtripvolumesandhighly
standardized service demand. As autonomous systems reach commercial reliability in these high-density
operating environments, Robotaxis gain access to a market large enough to support scaled, platform-level
businessesratherthanisolatedpilotprograms.
The core driver of Robotaxi economics is structural cost reduction. By removing the human driver,
Robotaxi operations eliminate what is typically the single largest expense in traditional ride-hailing: labor
cost. In many markets, driver compensation accounts for the overwhelming majority of per-trip operating
costs. In parallel, the industry is moving from retrofitted autonomous vehicles to factory-integrated
autonomous platforms, which is expected to reduce upfront vehicle costs, improve hardware consistency
andenhancesystemreliability.
As a result, once deployed at scale, Robotaxi operations are expected to deliver meaningful margin
expansion in China, with even stronger margin potentialin markets facing acutelaborshortagesandhigher
laborcostssuchasUnitedArabEmirates,UnitedStates,andEurope.
Although still at an early stage of large-scale deployment, Robotaxi services are approaching broader
commercial use as system performance improves and regulatory frameworks continue to evolve. Though
the globaland China’s RobotaxioperationsmarketswerearoundUS$0.1 billionin2025, theyareexpected
to expand to approximately US$81.8 billion globally and US$38.1 billion in China by 2030, reflecting the
transitionfrompilotprogramstoscaledcommercialnetworks.Meanwhile,by2030,Robotaxipenetrationis
projectedtoreachapproximately5.7%globallyand11.9%inChina.

CompetitiveLandscapeoftheRobotaxiMarket
At present, global Robotaxi competition is broadly shaped by two distinct operating models, which
differfundamentallyinhowtechnologyisdeveloped,deployedandscaled.
• “Tesla-style”mass-production-baseddata-drivenmodel:Onegroupofplayersleverageslarge
installedbasesofmass-producedvehiclestocollectreal-worlddrivingdataonacontinuousbasis.
These companies improve system performance primarily through large-scale data-driven
reinforcment learning model, free from pre-built high-definition maps. Because data is gathered
organically from mass-produced vehicles operating across many locations, this model supports
faster geographic scaling, lower marginal expansion cost and more predictable rollout timelines.
As performance improves through data accumulation,these systems can be replicatedacross new
regionswithfewerlocation-specificmodifications.Thismodelprioritizessoftwarescalabilityand
data compounding, with competitive advantage driven largely by fleet size, data density and
algorithm iteration speed. A representative example of this approach is Tesla, which relies on its
globalproductionfleetastheprimarydataenginefordrivingautomationdevelopment.
• “Waymo-style” dedicated fleet model: The second group of players operates modified Robotaxi
fleets within approved pilot cities. These companies typically deploy vehicles that often rely on
detailed, location-specific map and on-site system calibration. Expansion under this model features
significant engineering and operational resources required to validate each new geography before
commercial launch. This model tends to achieve deep technical optimization within tightly
controlledoperatingareas,butrequireshigherupfrontcapitalinvestment,longerdeploymentcycles
and greater local customization. As a result, geographic expansion is usually more deliberate, time
consuming and capital-intensive. A typical example of this model is Waymo, which operates
dedicated Robotaxi services supported by detailed city mapping and on-site system calibration.
Waymo is an driving automation company originally incubated within Alphabet and one of the
earliestcommercialoperatorsoffullydriverlessRobotaxiservicesintheUnitedStates.

KeySuccessFactorsforRobotaxiServices
At the heart of the Robotaxi Services is the scalability that turns pilots into rapid deployments. In this
early stage of commercialization, the winner is who can scale with massive acceleration. That means
expanding from a handful of routes to even hundred of thousands of fleets or even more, from one city to
many,andfromasingleuse casetoawideningsetofscenarios.Thisscalabilityisanchoredinaninterplay
of capabilities including safety, cost economics, rapid generalization, and a strong partnership ecosystem,
whichtogetherdeterminewhocompoundsfasterandultimatelyemergesasamarketleader.

Safety and reliability: A demonstrably superior safety record, proven over millions of miles, is a
prerequisitefor regulatoryacceptanceandconsumeradoption.Thisrequiresaccessanduseofcontinuously
expanding real-world driving dataset that supports system training, validation and stress testing across rare
andcomplexcornercases.
Cost efficiency: Achieving leadership in the sector demands a fundamental advantage in cost
efficiency. This is driven by mass-produced production scale and the ability to reuse large volumes of
NOA-derived driving data across multiple applications. Together, these factors lower per-vehicle hardware
costsandimprovefleet-leveluniteconomics,enablingprofitableexpansionatscale.
Rapid generalization across cities and operating environments: The abilityto expand efficientlyinto
new cities is a decisive competitiveadvantage in scalable robotics. This depends on a data-driventechnical
architecture that minimizesreliance on heavy location-specificcustomization, as well as the reuse of mass-
productionhardwareplatformstokeepdeploymentcostsundercontrol.Together,thesecapabilitiessupport
faster,morecapital-efficientgeographicexpansion.
Operational partnerships as the gateway to rapid commercialization: Deep cooperation with OEMs,
fleet operators and mobility platforms provides immediate access to commercial operating channels and
real-world deployment environments. Large-scale closed-loop driving data accumulated from these
deployments serves as the primary value exchange, accelerating partner success, strengthening long-term
commercialrelationshipsandcontinuouslyimprovingsystemperformance.
StrategicPositioningfortheNextStageofFullAutonomy
Over the long term, the wealth of real-world dataset sets the upper bound of driving automation
performance and commercial success. Large, continuously growing real-world datasets accelerate algorithm
improvement,raisefunctionalsafetythresholds,enablerepeatablecross-cityandcross-platformdeployment,and
ultimatelydeterminewhichplayersemergeaslong-termwinnersonthepathtowardfullautonomy.
In the next phase of industry evolution, the market is likely to consolidate further. Leadership will
increasingly concentrate among companies that combine mass-production data generation, platform-based
technical architectures and broad partner integration capabilities are expected to hold a decisive advantage.
Together, these elements form a self-reinforcing cycle in which rare corner cases are continuously
accumulated,systemperformanceimprovesatafasterpace,deploymentcostsdecline,andmarketadoption
acceleratesacrossbothmass-producedvehiclesanddedicatedautonomousfleets.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
This section sets forth a summary of the major rules and regulations that may affect our business

RegulationsRelatedtoForeignInvestment
Theestablishment,operationandmanagementofcompaniesinChinaaremainlygovernedbythePRC
Company Law (《中華人民共和國公司法》), which was last amended in December 2023 and came into
effect in July 2024. The PRC Company Law applies to both domestic companies and foreign-invested
companies. On March 15, 2019, the NPC approved the Foreign Investment Law (《中華人民共和國外商投
資法》), which took effect on January 1, 2020. Pursuant to the Foreign Investment Law, “foreign
investments” refer to investment activities conducted by foreign investors (including foreign natural
persons, foreign enterprises or other foreign organizations) directly or indirectly in the PRC, which include
any of the following circumstances: (i) foreign investors setting up foreign-invested enterprises in the PRC
solely or jointly with other investors, (ii) foreign investors obtaining shares, equity interests, property
portions or other similar rights and interests of enterprises within the PRC, (iii) foreign investors investing
in new projects in the PRC solely or jointly with other investors and (iv) investment in other methods as
specifiedinlawsoradministrativeregulations,orasstipulatedbytheStateCouncil.
The Foreign Investment Law and its implementing rules provide that a system of pre-entry national
treatment and negative list shall be applied for the administration of foreign investment, where “pre-entry
nationaltreatment”meansthatthetreatmentgiventoforeigninvestorsandtheirinvestmentsatmarketaccess
stageisnolessfavorablethanthatgiventodomesticinvestorsandtheirinvestments,and“negativelist”means
the special administrative measures for foreign investment’s access to specific fields or industries. Foreign
investment beyond the negative list will be granted national treatment. The most recently amended industry
entryclearancerequirementsgoverninginvestmentactivitiesinthePRCbyforeigninvestorsaresetoutintwo
categories,namelytheSpecialAdministrativeMeasures(NegativeList)fortheAccessofForeignInvestment
(2024 version) (《外商投資准入特別管理措施(負面清單)(2024年版)》), as promulgated by the NDRC and the
MOFCOM and taking effect on November 1, 2024, and the Encouraged Industry Catalog for Foreign
Investment (2025 version) (《鼓勵外商投資產業目錄(2025年版)》), as promulgated by the NDRC and the
MOFCOM and taking effect on February 1, 2026. Industries not listed in the Negative List are generally
deemed“permitted”forforeigninvestmentunlessspecificallyrestrictedbyotherPRClaws.
Pursuant to the Foreign Investment Law and its implementing rules, and the Measures on Foreign
Investment Information Reporting (《外商投資信息報告辦法》) jointly promulgated by the MOFCOM and
the SAMR, which took effect on January 1, 2020, a foreign investment information reporting system shall
be established and foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises shall report investment information to
competent commerce departments of the government through the enterprise registration system and the
enterprise credit information publicity system, and the administration for market regulation shall forward
the above investment information to the competentcommercedepartmentsin a timelymanner. The foreign
investors or foreign-invested enterprises shall report the investment information by submitting reports
includinginitialreports,changereports,deregistrationreportsandannualreports,etc.
OnDecember19,2020,theNDRCandtheMOFCOMjointlypromulgatedtheMeasuresfortheSecurity
Review of Foreign Investment (《外商投資安全審查辦法》), which became effective on January 18, 2021.
Accordingtothesemeasures,foreigninvestorsorrelevantpartiesinthePRCshalltaketheinitiativetomakea
declarationontheirinvestmentsforsecurityreviewtothecompetentauthoritypriorto(i)makinginvestments
inthemilitaryindustry,militaryindustrialsupportandotherfieldsrelatingtothesecurityofnationaldefense,
and investments in areas surrounding military facilities and military industry facilities; and (ii) obtaining
controloverenterprisesinvolvedinimportantagriculturalproducts,importantenergyandresources,important
equipment manufacturing, important infrastructure, important transport services, important cultural products
and services, important information technologies and internet products and services, important financial
services,keytechnologiesandotherimportantfieldsrelatingtonationalsecurity.

RegulationsRelatedtoDrivingAutomationandIntelligentConnectedVehicles
TheTaxonomyofDrivingAutomationforVehicles(《汽車駕駛自動化分級》)waspromulgatedbythe
SAMR and Standardization Administration on August 20, 2021 and became effective on March 1, 2022,
which refers to the internationally recognized SAE J3016 classification framework and stipulates that the
standards for driving automation can be divided into six levels: Level 0 (emergency assistance), Level 1
(partial driver assistance), Level 2 (combined driver assistance), Level 3 (conditionallyautomated driving),
Level4(highlyautomateddriving)andLevel5(fullyautomateddriving).Specifically,Level0requiresthe
system to have the capability to continuously perform detection and response of a part of the object and
event, and when the driver requests the exit of the assisted driving system, the control right of the system
should be immediately released. Both Level 1 and Level 2 require the assisted driving system to
continuously perform vehicle lateral or longitudinal motion control in a dynamic driving task and require
the system to have a partial capability of object and event detection and response in accordance with the
vehiclelateralorlongitudinalmotioncontrol.Level3mainlyrequiresthatthedrivingautomationsystembe
able to perform the full range of dynamic driving tasks under its designed operating conditions after
activation. Level 4 mainly requires that the driving automation system should, apart from performing the
full range of dynamic driving tasks under its designed operating conditions, be able to automatically
implementtheriskmitigationstrategytoreachtheminimizedriskstatewhenrelevanteventsoccur,andthe
userdoesnotrespondtotheinterventionrequest.Furthermore,Level5requiresthatthedrivingautomation
systemhasnolimitationonthedesignedoperatingrange(exceptforcommercialandregulatoryconstraints)
andisabletoachievefullyautomateddriving.
On February25, 2025, theMinistryof Industry andInformationTechnology(MIIT) issuedanoticeto
further strengthen the administration of access, recall, and Over-the-Air (OTA) upgrades for intelligent
connected vehicle products. The notice mandates that additional technical parameters, including those
related to combined driving assistance systems and OTA upgrade information, be incorporated into the
main technical parameters table of vehicle products. This requirement is designed to enhance the MIIT’s
oversight of product access and production consistency. Furthermore, these parameters must be filed with
the State Administration for Market Regulation, ensuring the effective implementation of vehicle product
defect investigations and recall procedures. Furthermore, the government authorities have emphasized that
2026 marks the beginning of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, during which the intelligent connected new
energy vehicle industry is expected to enter a pivotal phase for high-quality development. The government
authorities aim to accelerate advancements in technologies such as high-level autonomous driving and
furtherstimulateautomobileconsumption.
According to the Announcement on Extending and Optimizing the Vehicle Purchase Tax Exemption
Policy for New Energy Vehicles (《關於延續和優化新能源汽車車輛購置稅減免政策的公告》) (the “Tax
Exemption Announcement”) issued by the Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration, and MIIT
inJune2023,thevehiclepurchasetaxexemptionpolicyfornewenergyvehicleswillbemodifiedfroma“full
exemption”toa“50%exemption,”cappedatRMB15,000pervehicle,effectiveJanuary1,2026.
In addition, there have been recentmediareports thatPRC authoritiesmay havesuspended or delayed
the issuance of new autonomous driving permits following recent service outages involving robotaxi
operationsinChina.Asofthedateofthisprospectus,wearenotawareofanyofficialnotice,ruleorpublic
announcement issued by PRC authorities confirming such suspension or delay. Accordingly, the Company
does not believe such media reports, by themselves, evidence any formal change in the applicable
regulatoryrequirements.
Weconsiderthattheregulatorydevelopmentsoutlinedabovewillnothaveamaterialadverseeffecton
our business, financial condition, or results of operations. In reaching this conclusion, we have taken into
account the following factors: (i) the MIIT notice introduces stricter requirements for access, recall, and
OTA upgrades, but it is expected to drive long-term high-quality development within the autonomous
driving industry; (ii) while the Tax Exemption Announcement may increase upfront costs for end
consumers and cause short-term fluctuations in orders, the advance announcement allows the market to
–110–

RegulationsonRoadTestingandDemonstrativeApplicationofIntelligentConnectedVehicles
The Administrative Norms for Road Testing and Demonstrative Application of Intelligent Connected
Vehicles (for Trial Implementation) (《智能網聯汽車道路測試與示範應用管理規範(試行)》), or the Road
Testing and Demonstrative Application Norms, as promulgated by the MIIT, the Ministry of Public
Security (the “MPS”) and the Ministry of Transport on July 27, 2021, and taking effect on September 1,
2021, is the primary regulation governing protocol of road testing and demonstration application of
intelligent connected vehicles in the PRC. Pursuant to the Road Testing and Demonstrative Application
Norms, the road testing means the autonomous driving function testing of intelligent connected vehicles
conducted on the designated sections of various roads for the passage of social motor vehicles; while the
demonstration application is referred to as the pilot and experimental operation of carrying passengers or
goodsbyintelligentconnectedvehiclesonthedesignatedsectionsofvariousroadsforthepassageofpublic
motorvehicles.Anyentityintendingtoconducttheroadtestinganddemonstrationapplicationofintelligent
connected vehicles must provide the safety self-statement which shall be confirmed by the relevant
competent governmental departments at the provincial or municipal level and apply for and obtain a
temporary license plate for each tested vehicle. The duration for a road testing and a demonstration
application shall not exceed 18 months in principle and should not exceed the validity period of the
certificateofsafetytechnicalinspectionandtheinsurancevoucherofthetestedvehicle.
Toqualifyforconductingtheroadtestingand/ordemonstrationapplication,anapplicantentitymustsatisfy,
among others, the following requirements: (i) it must be an independent legal person registered under the PRC
law with relevant business capacities relating to intelligent connected vehicles, such as manufacturing of
automobiles and automobile parts, technology research and development, experiment and testing and sufficient

connected vehicles, which has established protocols to test and assess the performance of driving automation
functionalities of intelligent connected vehicles; and (ii) it shall be capable of conducting real-time remote
monitor of the vehicles, and has the ability to record, analyze and reproduce events related to vehicles and to
ensure the network security of vehicles and remote monitoring platform. In addition, as to the demonstration
application,theapplicantentitycouldalsobeaconsortiumofseveralindependentlegalpersons,atleastoneof
