RegulationsonRoadTrafficSafetyofIntelligentConnectedVehicles
The Road Traffic Safety Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國道路交通安全法》) enacted by the
Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on October 28, 2003 and most recently amended
and became effective on April 29, 2021, sets out the basic framework for road traffic safety and provides
the rules for the drivers of vehicles, pedestrians, passengers and entities and individuals involved in road
traffic activities. Pursuant to the Road Traffic Safety Law of the PRC, in the event of any traffic accident
which causes personal injury or property damage, the insurance company shall make compensation within
the coverage of the compulsory third-partyliabilityinsurance and the shortfall shall be borne by the parties
involvedaccordingtotheirrespectivefaultdegree.
The Road Testing and Demonstrative Application Norms set out that on the occurrence of any
traffic violation or traffic accident during road testing or demonstrative application, the traffic
administrative department shall handle it in accordance with road traffic safety laws and regulations. In
the case of a car accident causing severe injury or death of personnel or vehicle damage, the applicant
must report the accident to the competent provincial or municipal government department within
twenty-four hours via the information system, or else its road testing or demonstrative application
activities may be suspended for twenty-four months. Furthermore, the applicant must submit in writing
the cause of accident, liability determination results and a comprehensive accident analysis report to
the relevant competent government department within five working days after the liability for the
accident has been determined.
The Access and On-road Traffic Guidelines further clarify how liability should be handled when road
trafficaccidentsoccuramongon-roadtrafficofintelligentconnectedvehicles.Specifically,wheretheaccident

RegulationsRelatedtoCybersecurityandDataSecurity
The Decision in Relation to Protection of Internet Security (《全國人民代表大會常務委員會關於維護互
聯網安全的決定》) enacted by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of the PRC on
December 28, 2000, as amended in August 2009, provides that, among other things, the following
cybersecurity, data security and privacy related activities conducted through the internet, if constituting a
criminal act under PRC laws, are subject to criminal punishment: (i) invading any computer information
system in the realm of state affairs, national defense or the cutting-edge science and technology;
(ii) intentionally inventing and spreading destructive programs such as computer viruses to attack the
computer system and the communications network, thus damaging the computer system and the
communications networks; (iii) in violation of state regulations, discontinuing the computer network or the
communicationsservicewithoutauthorization,asaresultofwhichthecomputernetworkorcommunication
systemcannotfunctionproperly;(iv)stealingorleakingstatesecrets,intelligenceormilitarysecretsviathe
Internet;(v) illegallyintercepting,tamperingwith,ordeletinganyemailoranyotherdataofanyperson,or
otherwiseinfringingonanycitizen’srighttofreedomandprivacyofcorrespondence,etc.
The Administrative Measures on the Security Protection of Computer Information Network with
International Connections (《計算機信息網絡國際聯網安全保護管理辦法》), issued by the MPS in
December 1997 and amended by the State Council in January 2011, prohibit the use of the Internet in a
manner that would result in the leakage of state secrets or the spread of socially destabilizing content. The

OnJuly1,2015,theStandingCommitteeoftheNationalPeople’sCongressofthePRCissuedtheNational

The Cybersecurity Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國網絡安全法》), or the PRC Cybersecurity Law,
which was promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of the PRC on
November 7, 2016 and most recently amended on October 28, 2025 and came into effect on January 1,
2026,appliestotheconstruction,operation,maintenanceanduseofnetworksaswellasthesupervisionand
administration of cybersecurity in China. The PRC Cybersecurity Law defines “networks” as systems that
are composed of computers or other information terminals and relevant facilities used for the purpose of
collecting, storing, transmitting, exchanging and processing information in accordance with certain rules
and procedures. “Network operators,” who are broadly defined as owners and administrators of networks
and network service providers, are subject to security protection obligations in accordance with multiple-
level protection scheme in relation to cybersecurity and various security protection-related obligations,
including: (i) formulating the internal security management rules and manual, appointing cybersecurity
responsible personnel; (ii) adopting technical measures to prevent computer viruses, cyber-attacks,
intrusions and other and cybersecurity endangering activities; (iii) adopting technical measures to monitor
and record network operation status and cybersecurity security incidents and maintain internet logs for no
less than six months; (iv) adopting data classification, data back-up and encryption and other measures;
(v) formulating cybersecurity emergency response plans, timely handling security risks, initiating
emergency response plans immediately after the cybersecurity incident, taking appropriate remedial
measures and reporting to regulatory authorities. Network operators who do not comply with the security
protection obligations in PRC Cybersecurity Law may be subject to rectification order, warning and fines.
Inaddition,thePRCCybersecurityLawimposescertainadditionalrequirementsontheCriticalInformation
Infrastructure Operators, or the CIIOs, including that during their operations in the PRC, CIIOs should
generally store the personal information and important data collected and produced within the territory of
mainlandChinaandperformcertainsecurityobligations.

and individualscarrying outdataactivities.TheDataSecurityLawalsointroducesadataclassificationand

theaccompaniedClassificationandCategorizationGuideforCybersecurityIncidentsclassifycybersecurity

operators (other than CIIOs) shall report incidents of relatively serious level or above to the cyberspace
administration at the provincial level of their locality within four hours. Network operators may submit
reports through the 12387 hotline, website, e-mail, fax or other channels. Where an operator fails to fulfill
its reporting obligations under the Cybersecurity Incidents Reporting Measures, or delays, omits,
mis-reports or conceals cybersecurity incidents and thereby causes material harmful consequences, the
cyberspace administration will impose heavier penalties on the operator and the relevant liable persons in
accordancewithapplicablelaw;operatorsthathaveadoptedreasonableprotectivemeasuresandreportedin
atimelymannerasrequiredmaybesubjecttolighterormitigatedpenalties,orbeexemptedfrompenalties.

shall be a voluntary and explicit indication of intent given by such individual on a fully informed basis. If
lawsoradministrativeregulationsprovidethattheprocessingofpersonalinformationshallbesubjecttothe
separate consent or written consent of the individual concerned, such provisions shall prevail. Personal
information processors shall be responsible for their personal information processing activities and take
necessary measures to ensure the security of the personal informationprocessed. Furthermore, the Personal

cyberspace administration has been entered into with the overseas recipient; or (iv) any other condition
prescribed by laws, administrative regulations or any other requirements by the national cyberspace
administration.

RegulationsRelatedtoIntellectualProperty
Patent
Patents in the PRC are principally protected under the Patent Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國專
利法》), or the Patent Law, promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of
the PRC on March 12, 1984, with the latest amendment taking effect on June 1, 2021, and the
Implementation Rules of the Patent Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國專利法實施細則》), or the
Implementation Rules of the Patent Law, promulgated by the State Council on June 15, 2001 and as most
recently amended on December 11, 2023 and effective on January 20, 2024, the patent administrative
department under the State Council is responsible for the administration of patent-related work nationwide
and the patent administration departments of provincial or autonomous regions or municipal governments
are responsible for administering patents within the respective administrative areas. The Patent Law and
Implementation Rules of the Patent Law provide for three types of patents, namely “inventions,” “utility
models” and “designs.” Invention patents are valid for twenty years, utility model patents are valid for ten
years,andsinceJune1,2021,thevalidationperiodfordesignpatentswhoseapplicationdateisafterJune1,
2021 are extended to fifteen years in each case from the date of application. The Chinese patent system
adopts a “first come, first file” principle, which means that where more than one person files a patent
application for the same invention, a patent will be granted to the person who files the applicationfirst. An
inventionorautilitymodelmustpossessnovelty,inventivenessandpracticalapplicabilitytobepatentable.
Thirdpartiesmustobtainconsentoraproperlicensefromthepatentownertousethepatent.Otherwise,the
unauthorizeduseconstitutesaninfringementonpatentrights.
Copyright
Copyright in the PRC, including copyrighted software, is principally protected under the Copyright
Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國著作權法》), or the Copyright Law, promulgated by the Standing
CommitteeoftheNationalPeople’sCongressofthePRConSeptember7,1990andmostrecentlyamended
on November 11, 2020 and effective on June 1, 2021, and related rules and regulations. Under the
Copyright Law, the term of protection for copyrighted software is fifty years. The Regulations on the
ProtectionoftheRighttoCommunicateWorkstothePublicoverInformationNetworks(《信息網絡傳播權
保護條例》), as most recently amended on January 30, 2013, provides specific rules on fair use, statutory
license, and a safe harbor for use of copyrights and copyright management technology and specifies the
liabilities of various entities for violations, including copyright holders, libraries and internet service
providers. The Computer Software Copyright Registration Measures (《計算機軟件著作權登記辦法》),
promulgatedbytheNationalCopyrightAdministrationonFebruary20,2002andlastamendedonJune18,
2004, regulate registrations of software copyrights, exclusive licensing contracts for software copyrights
and assignment agreements. The National Copyright Administration administers software copyright
registration and the Copyright Protection Center of China are designated as the software registration
authority.TheCopyrightProtectionCenterofChinagrantsregistrationcertificatestothecomputersoftware
copyrightsapplicantswhichmeettherelevantrequirements.

RegulationsRelatedtoEmployment,SocialInsuranceandHousingFund
AccordingtotheLaborContractLawofthePeople’sRepublicofChina(《中華人民共和國勞動合同法
》),ortheLaborContractLaw,promulgatedbytheStandingCommitteeoftheNationalPeople’sCongress
onJune29,2007andamendedonDecember28,2012,andtheImplementationRulesoftheLaborContract
Law of the People’s Republic of China (《中華人民共和國勞動合同法實施條例》), or the Implementation
Rules of the Labor Contract Law, promulgated by the State Council on September 18, 2008, a written
employmentcontractshallbeconcludedintheestablishmentofanemploymentrelationship.Ifanemployer
fails to enter into a written employmentcontract with an employee within one year from the date on which
theemploymentrelationshipisestablished,theemployermustrectifythesituationbyenteringintoawritten
employment contract with the employee and pay the employee twice the employee’s salary for the period
from the day following the lapse of one month from the date of establishment of the employment
relationship to the day prior to the execution of the written employment contract. The Labor Contract Law
and its implementationrules also require compensation to be paid upon certain terminations. In addition, if
an employer intends to enforce a non-compete provision in an employment contract or non-competition
agreement with an employee, it has to compensate the employee on a monthly basis during the term of the
restriction period after the termination or expiry of the labor contract. Employers in most cases are also
required to provide severance payment to their employees after their employment relationships are
terminated.
Employers in the PRC are required to contribute, for and on behalf of their employees, to a series of
social insurance funds, including funds for pension, unemployment insurance, medical insurance, work-
related injury insurance, maternity insurance, and housing funds. These payments are made to local
administrativeauthoritiesandemployerswhofailtocontributemaybefinedandorderedtomakeupforthe
outstanding contributions. The main laws and regulations that govern the employers’ obligations to
contribute to the social insurance funds include: the Social Insurance Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國
社會保險法》), which was promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress on
October 28, 2010 and amended with immediate effect on December 29, 2018, the Interim Regulations on
the Collection and Payment of Social Insurance Premiums (《社會保險費徵繳暫行條例》), which was
promulgated by the State Council on January 22, 1999, and amended with immediate effect on March 24,
2019,theRegulationsonWork-relatedInjuryInsurance(《工傷保險條例》),whichwaspromulgatedbythe
StateCouncilon April 27, 2003 and amendedonDecember20, 2010, andtheRegulationsonManagement
of the Housing Fund (《住房公積金管理條例》), which was promulgated on April 3, 1999, and was most
recentlyamendedwithimmediateeffectonMarch24,2019.

RegulationsRelatedtoForeignExchangeandDividendDistribution
RegulationsonForeignCurrencyExchange
The principal regulations governing foreign currency exchange in China are the Foreign Exchange
Administration Regulations (《中華人民共和國外匯管理條例》), most recently amended in 2008. Under
PRC foreign exchange regulations, payments of current account items, such as profit distributions, interest
payments and trade and service-related foreign exchange transactions, can be made in foreign currencies
without prior approval from SAFE, by complying with certain procedural requirements. By contrast,
approval from or registration with appropriate government authorities is required where RMB is to be
converted into foreign currency and remitted out of China to pay capital account items, such as direct
investments,repaymentofforeigncurrency-denominatedloans,repatriationofinvestmentsandinvestments
insecuritiesoutsideofChina.
In November 2012, SAFE promulgated the Circular of Further Improving and Adjusting Foreign
Exchange Administration Policies on Direct Investment (《關於進一步改進和調整直接投資外匯管理政策
的通知》), or Circular 59, which substantially amends and simplifies the current foreign exchange
procedure.PursuanttoCircular59, theopeningof variousspecialpurpose foreignexchangeaccounts,such
as pre-establishment expenses accounts, foreign exchange capital accounts and guarantee accounts, the
reinvestmentofRMBproceedsderivedbyforeigninvestorsinthePRC,andremittanceofforeignexchange
profits and dividends by a foreign-invested enterprise to its foreign shareholders no longer require the
approval or verification of SAFE, and multiple capital accounts for the same entity may be opened in
differentprovinces,whichwasnotpossiblepreviously.
In March 2015, SAFE promulgated the Circular on Reforming the Management Approach regarding
the Settlement of Foreign Capital of Foreign-invested Enterprise (《關於改革外商投資企業外匯資本金結匯
管理方式的通知》), or Circular 19, which expands a pilot reform of the administration of the settlement of
the foreign exchange capitals of foreign-invested enterprises nationwide. Circular 19 allows all foreign-
invested enterprises established in the PRC to settle their foreign exchange capital on a discretionary basis
according to the actual needs of their business operation, provides the procedures for foreign invested
companies to use Renminbi converted from foreign currency-denominated capital for equity investments.
However, Circular 19 continues to prohibit foreign-invested enterprises from, among other things, using
RMB funds converted from their foreign exchange capital for expenditure beyond their business scope,
direct or indirect securities investment and providing entrusted loans or repaying loans between
nonfinancialenterprises.SAFEpromulgatedtheNoticeoftheStateAdministrationofForeignExchangeon
Reforming and Standardizing the Foreign Exchange Settlement Management Policy of Capital Account
(《關於改革和規範資本項目結匯管理政策的通知》), or Circular 16, effective June 2016, which reiterates
some of the rules set forth in Circular 19. Circular 16 provides that discretionary foreign exchange
settlement applies to foreign exchange capital, foreign debt offering proceeds and remitted foreign listing
proceeds, and the corresponding RMB capital converted from foreign exchange may be used to extend
loans to related parties or repay inter-company loans (including advances by third parties). However,
Circular 16’s interpretation and implementation in practice may continue to evolve and subject to
uncertainties.Circular19orCircular16maydelayorlimitusfromusingtheproceedsofoffshoreofferings
to make additional capital contributions to our PRC subsidiaries and any violations of these circulars could
resultinseveremonetaryorotherpenalties.

RegulationsonDividendDistributions
The principal laws, rules and regulations governing dividends distribution by companies in the PRC
are the PRC Company Law, which applies to both domestic companies and foreign-invested companies,

and the Foreign Investment Law and its implementing rules, which apply to foreign-invested companies.
Under these laws, regulations and rules, both domestic companies and foreign-invested companies in the

amount of their reserves reaches 50% of their registered capital. PRC companies are not permitted to

RegulationsonOverseasInvestment
On December 26, 2017, the NDRC promulgated the Administrative Measures for the Outbound
Investment of Enterprises (《企業境外投資管理辦法》), which took effect on March 1, 2018 and requires
that non-sensitive overseas investment projects make record filings with the localbranch of the NDRC. On
September 6, 2014, the MOFCOM promulgated the Administrative Measures on Overseas Investments
(《境外投資管理辦法》), which took effect on October 6, 2014 and requires that overseas investments of
PRC enterprises that involve non-sensitive countries and regions and non-sensitive industries must make
record filings with a local branch of MOFCOM. Pursuant to Circular 59, PRC enterprises must register for
overseasdirectinvestmentwithlocalbanks.
In 2014, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the PRC (中華人民共和國國家外匯管理局)
issued the SAFE Circular on Relevant Issues Relating to Domestic Resident’s Investment and Financing and
Roundtrip Investment through Special Purpose Vehicles (《關於境內居民通過特殊目的公司境外投融資及返程
投資外匯管理有關問題的通知》), or SAFECircular 37. SAFECircular 37regulates foreignexchangematters
inrelationtotheuseofspecialpurposevehiclesbyPRCresidentsorentitiestoseekoffshoreinvestmentand
financing or conduct round trip investment in China. Under SAFE Circular 37, a “special purpose vehicle”
referstoanoffshoreentityestablishedorcontrolled,directlyorindirectly,byPRCresidentsorentitiesforthe
purpose of seeking offshore financing or making offshore investment, using legitimate onshore or offshore
assets or interests, while “round trip investment” refers to direct investment in China by PRC residents or
entities through special purpose vehicles, namely, establishing foreign-invested enterprises to obtain
ownership, control rights and management rights. SAFE Circular 37 provides that, before making a
contribution into a special purpose vehicle, PRC residents or entities are required to complete foreign
exchange registration with SAFE or its local branch. In 2015, SAFE promulgated the SAFE Circular on
FurtherSimplifyingandImprovingForeignExchangeAdministrationPolicyonDirectInvestment,amending
SAFECircular 37byrequiringPRCresidents or entities toregister withqualifiedbanksratherthanSAFEor
its local branch in connection with their establishment or control of an offshore entity established for the
purposeofoverseasinvestmentorfinancing.
On May 5, 2026, the State Council promulgated the Provisions of the State Council on Overseas
Investment (《國務院關於對外投資的規定》), which will take effect on July 1, 2026, which applies to
domestic enterprises, other organizations and individual residents conducting overseas investment. It
improves the overseas investment security review system, and prohibits the illegal cross-border transfer of
goods, technologies, services and data that are prohibited or restricted from export. It also clarifies the
compliance obligations including filing, information reporting and cross-border fund management for
overseasinvestmentactivities.

RegulationsRelatedtoTax
EnterpriseIncomeTax
The PRC EIT is calculated based on the taxable income determined under the applicable EIT Law
(《中華人民共和國企業所得稅法》), and its implementation rules, both of which became effective in
January 2008 and were most recently amended in December 2018 and December 2024, respectively. The
EITLawgenerallyimposesauniformenterpriseincometaxrateof25%onallresidententerprisesinChina,
includingforeign-investedenterprises.
The EIT Law and its implementation rules permit certain High and New Technologies Enterprises to
enjoy a reduced 15% enterprise income tax rate if they meet certain criteria and are officially
acknowledged.
Value-addedTax
On December 25, 2024, the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress promulgated the
Value-added Tax Law (《中華人民共和國增值稅法》), which took effect on January 1, 2026 and replaced
the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax of the PRC. Pursuant to the Value-added Tax Law,
entities engaged in the sale of goods, services, intangible assets and immovables and importation of goods
withintheterritoryofthePRCareVATpayersandshallpayVAT.Taxpayersthatsellgoodsaresubjectto
ataxrateof 13% andtaxpayersthatsellservicesor intangibleassetsaresubjecttoataxrateof6%.Unless
otherwise specified in the Value-added Tax Law, taxpayers making taxable transactions shall calculate and
pay VAT by offsetting input tax against output tax according to the general tax calculation method and
calculatetheVATpayable.

overseas listingor offering by a PRC domesticcompany is explicitlyprohibitedunder any of thefollowing

SanctionsLawsandRegulations
UnitedStates
The Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”) is the primary agency responsible for administering
U.S. sanctions programmes against targeted countries, entities, and individuals. “Primary” U.S. sanctions
apply to “U.S. persons” or activities involving a U.S. nexus (e.g., funds transfers in U.S. currency even if
performed by non-U.S. persons), and “secondary” U.S. sanctions apply extraterritoriallyto the activities of
non-U.S.personsevenwhenthetransactionhasnoU.S.nexus.
Depending on the sanctions program and/or parties involved, U.S. law also may require a U.S.
companyoraU.S.personto“block”(freeze)anyassets/propertyinterestsowned,controlledorheldforthe
benefit of a sanctioned country, entity, or individual when such assets/property interests are in the United
States or within the possession or control of a U.S. person. Upon such blocking, no transaction may be
undertaken or effected with respect to the asset/property interest — no payments, benefits, provision of
servicesorotherdealingsorothertypeofperformance(incaseofcontracts/agreements)—exceptpursuant
toanauthorizationorlicensefromOFAC.
OFAC’scomprehensivesanctionsprogrammescurrentlyapplytoCuba,Iran,NorthKorea,theCrimea
region of Russia/Ukraine, and the self-proclaimed Luhansk People’s Republic (“LPR”) and Donetsk
People’s Republic (“DPR”) regions (the comprehensive OFAC sanctions programme against Sudan was
terminated on October 12, 2017). OFAC also prohibits virtually all business dealings with persons and
entitiesidentifiedintheSDNList.EntitiesthatapartyontheSDNListowns(definedasadirectorindirect
ownershipinterestof50%ormore,individuallyorintheaggregate)arealsoblocked,regardlessofwhether
thatentityisexpresslynamedontheSDNList.

U.S.ExportControls
The United States has implemented and has proposed additional restrictions, some of which may
impact Chinese companies, including us. The United States has increased export controls restrictions on
ChinathroughtheExportAdministrationRegulations(the“EAR”),administeredbytheBureauofIndustry
and Security of the U.S. Department of Commerce (the “BIS”), which includes a list of foreign persons on
which certain trade restrictions are imposed (the “Entity List”). Where a foreign person is included on the
Entity List, the export, re-export and/or transfer (in-country) of items which are subject to the EAR
generallyisprohibitedunlessthespecifiedlicenserequirementsaremet.
In addition, EAR also maintains a list of items, software, and technology that are subject to export
controls (the “Commerce Control List”). BIS can also implement unilateral licensing requirements and
other controls on items subject to U.S. export controls jurisdiction that can restrict exports and reexports to
certain countries, as well as transfers within a country to a different end-user or end-use. The Commerce
ControlListisdividedintotencategories,representedbythefirstdigitoftheExportControlClassification
Number(“ECCN”).EachECCNissubjecttotherespectivecontrol(s)andlicensingrequirementapplicable
forsalestocontrolledcountriesand/orentities.

HISTORICALCONTRACTUALARRANGEMENTS
Historically, we conducted our business operations in the PRC through a series of contractual
arrangements, as amended, with Chusudu (Suzhou) Technology Co., Ltd. (初速度(蘇州)科技有限公司)
(“Suzhou Chusudu”) and Beijing Chusudu Technology Co., Ltd. (北京初速度科技有限公司) (“Beijing
Chusudu”,togetherwithSuzhouChusudu,the“FormerVIEs”)andtheirrespectiveregisteredshareholders,
throughwhichweobtainedcontrolovertheFormerVIEs.AlthoughSuzhouChusudu’sprincipalbusinesswas
technologyR&Dwhichdidnotfallintoanyrestrictedorprohibitedbusinessesunderthenegativelistpursuant
to the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國外商投資法》) (the “Negative List”), we
historically entered into contractual arrangements with it to preserve flexibility for it to potentially engage in
businesses subject to foreign investment restrictions or prohibitions based on actual business development
needsinthePRC.Besides,BeijingChusudu’sprincipalbusinesswastechnologyR&Dwhichdidnotfallinto
restricted or prohibited businesses under the Negative List, while it also conducted navigation electronic map
manufacturing business and held a corresponding surveying and mapping license to accelerate relevant
technology iterations. In addition, Beijing Chusudu held other surveying and mapping licenses covering
certain business in restricted or prohibited industries under the Negative List, including geographic
information systemengineering business whileitdidnotactuallyengageinsuchotherbusinesses.Therefore,
we historically also entered into contractual arrangements with Beijing Chusudu. Such historical contractual
arrangements entered into with respect to the Former VIEs allowed us to (i) have the power to direct the
operation and activities of the Former VIEs, (ii) receive substantially all of the economic benefits of the
Former VIEs, and (iii) have an exclusive option to purchase all or part of the equity interests in the Former
VIEs when and to the extent permitted by PRC laws. These contractual arrangements included technical
consultingandservicesagreements,sharepledgeagreements,exclusiveoptionagreements,powersofattorney
and spousal consents. As a result of these contractual arrangements, for accounting purposes, our Company
exerted effective control over, the Former VIEs and consolidated their operating results in our financial
statementsunderapplicableaccountingstandardsfortherelevantperiod.
Given that the surveying and mapping license covering navigation electronic map manufacturing
business expired in December 2021, and Beijing Chusudu voluntarily applied for and completed the
cancellationofothersurveyingandmappinglicensesinJanuary2024,havingevaluatedourbusinessplanthat
our operations are not in the restricted or prohibited industries under the Negative List and are not otherwise
limitedbyotherPRCforeigninvestmentlawsandregulations,andhavingconsideredthebenefitsofthedirect
equity ownership under applicable laws and regulations in preparation of the Listing, in January 2024, we
enteredintorespectiveterminationagreementsandequitytransferagreementswith,amongothers,theFormer
VIEs and their respective registered shareholders to terminate the aforementioned contractual arrangements
and acquire the entire equity interests in Suzhou Chusudu and Beijing Chusudu, following which each of
Suzhou Chusudu and Beijing Chusudu has become a wholly-owned subsidiary of our Company. As advised
bythePRCLegalAdviser,sinceBeijingChusuduhadceasedtoconducttherelevantsurveyingandmapping
activitiesbytheexpiryoftherelevantsurveyingandmappinglicenseinDecember2021,andtheFormerVIEs
had not engaged in any other restricted or prohibited business under the Negative List during the term of
contractual arrangements and following the termination of the contractual arrangements up to the Latest
PracticableDate,theGroup’soperationswerenotintherestrictedorprohibitedindustriesundertheNegative
ListduringtheTrackRecordPeriodanduptotheLatestPracticableDate.

RightsofthePre-IPOInvestors
The Pre-IPO Investors were granted customary special rights, including but not limited to the
redemptionright,informationright,rightoffirstrefusal,drag-alongrightand/ordirectorappointmentright.
TheredemptionrighthadbeenterminatedimmediatelybeforethesubmissionoftheListingapplication,but
shall automatically be reinstated upon the earlier occurrence of any of the following events: (a) where our
Company voluntarily withdraws the Listing application or no re-filing has been made for the Listing
application within six months after the lapse of such Listing application; (b) the rejection of the Listing
application by the relevant securities regulatory authority and/or stock exchange; and (c) the failure by our
Company to consummate a qualified initial public offering within 24 months after such submission of the
Listingapplication.AllotherspecialrightsgrantedtothePre-IPO Investors byour Companyshallceaseto
beeffectiveuponListing.
All Preferred Shares shall be automatically converted into Shares on a one-to-one basis upon
completionoftheGlobalOffering.
CompliancewiththePre-IPOInvestmentGuidance
Based on the documents provided by our Company relating to the Pre-IPO Investments, on the basis
that(i)theconsiderationforthePre-IPOInvestmentswassettledmorethan28cleardaysbeforethedateof
the first submission of the Listing application by our Company to the Stock Exchange (the “First Filing”),
(ii) the redemption rights granted to the Pre-IPO Investors were suspended prior to the First Filing, and
(iii) all other special rights granted to the Pre-IPO Investors shall be terminated upon Listing, the Joint
Sponsors confirm that the Pre-IPO Investments are in compliance with Chapter 4.2 of the Guide issued by
theStockExchange.

LISTINGPLANANDREASONSFORTHELISTING
Our Company evaluated different options for accessing international capital markets, including the
possibility of seeking an initial public offering in the United States. Our Company has submitted a draft
registration statement to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) in connection with a
potentiallisting in the United States (the “Contemplated U.S. Listing”), and has been engaged in multiple
rounds of review and comment exchanges with the SEC. The Contemplated U.S. Listing has been subject
to, among other things, prevailing market conditions, regulatory developments and our overall strategic
considerations. After taking into account, among other factors, (i) the Stock Exchange’s position as an
internationally recognized and reputable exchange, (ii) that we can access to a broad and diverse investor
base through the Listing, (iii) that the Global Offering can further our Group’s long-term development
strategy, and (iv) that the Listing can further enhance our brand profile and market visibility, our Directors
consider that a listing on the Stock Exchange would be a suitable option for our Group. Accordingly, we
voluntarilydecidedtofirstpursuealistinginHongKong.AsoftheLatestPracticableDate,therehadbeen
no disagreement between our Company and any professional parties engaged for the Contemplated U.S.
Listing. Our Directors further confirm that there is no other matter in relation to the Contemplated U.S.
ListingthatneedstobebroughttotheattentionoftheStockExchangeorpotentialinvestors.
Further, if we decide to further pursue the Contemplated U.S. Listing in the future, the Contemplated
U.S. Listing is expected to be a direct listing without issuance of any new Shares and therefore, the
shareholding of our Shareholders immediately following completion of the Global Offering will not be
dilutedasaresultoftheContemplatedU.S.Listing.
Based on the due diligence conducted by the Joint Sponsors, nothing has come to the Joint Sponsors’
attentionthatwouldreasonablycausethemtodisagreewiththeDirectors’viewthatthereisnoothermatter
inrelationtotheContemplatedU.S. ListingthatneedstobebroughttotheattentionoftheStockExchange
orpotentialinvestors.

asapercentageofthetotalnumberofSharesshallbe10%ineachcase.

M&ARules
According to the “Provisions Regarding Mergers and Acquisitions of Domestic Enterprises by Foreign
Investors”(《關於外國投資者併購境內企業的規定》)(the“M&ARules”)jointlyissuedbytheMOFCOM,the
State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council (國務院國有資產監督
管理委員會), the State Taxation Administration of the PRC (中華人民共和國國家稅務總局), the CSRC, the
SAMR and the SAFE, where a domestic company or natural person holds an equity interest in a domestic
company through an offshore special purpose company by paying the acquisition price with equity interests,
theoverseaslistingofthatspecialpurposecompanyshallbesubjecttoapprovalbytheCSRC.
AsadvisedbyourPRCLegalAdviser,priorCSRCapprovalundertheM&ARulesisnotrequiredfor
the Global Offering as the CSRC has not issued any definitive rule or interpretation concerning whether
offerings like ours under this prospectus are subject to the M&A Rules. Our PRC Legal Adviser further
advises that the possibility that relevant PRC governmental authorities, including the CSRC, would not
reachthesameconclusionasourPRCLegalAdvisercannotberuledout.
SAFERegistration

she contributes assets or equity interests in an overseas special purpose vehicle (the “Overseas SPV”) that
is directly established or controlled by the PRC resident for the purpose of conducting investment or
financing; and (b) following the initial registration, the PRC resident is required to register with the local
SAFEbranchforanymajorchangeinrespectoftheOverseasSPV.PursuanttothecircularoftheSAFEon
Further Simplification and Improvement in Foreign Exchange Administration on Direct Investment (《國
家外匯管理局關於進一步簡化和改進直接投資外匯管理政策的通知》), the power to accept SAFE registration
wasdelegatedfromlocalSAFEtolocalbanks.

WhoWeAre
We are a leading autonomous driving company in terms of both technological advancement and
commercial success. We ranked No. 1 among all independent driving automation solutions providers
globally in terms of both the sales volume of vehicles equipped with our Urban NOA solutions for the
trailing 12 months ended February 28, 2026, and the number of mass-produced vehicle models
incorporating our Urban NOA solutions as of February 28, 2026, according to CIC. We focus on
developing and commercializing driving automation technologies to improve safety and efficiency in
mobility and logistics, including through mass-produced vehicle solutions and scalable autonomous
mobility applications. We are currently at an early stage of deploying L3/L4 autonomous driving solutions
andarecontinuingtoadvancetowardhigherlevelsofautonomy.
Weoffertwosolutions:(i)thedeploymentofoursolutionsinmass-producedvehicles(“Solutionsfor
Mass-produced Vehicles”) and (ii) the development of a scalable, driverless AD mobility and logistics
business (“Solutions for Robotaxi Services”), with potential expansion into Robovan and Robotruck
services. L2 assisted driving could be divided into three categories according to the degree of autonomy:
L2-ADAS, L2-Highway NOA and L2-Urban NOA. In 2025, independent solution providers represented
28.3% and 33.4% of the global and China markets for L2-Highway NOA and L2-Urban NOA solutions,
respectively,intermsofsalesvolume.

strategy, as illustratedbythegraphicsbelow. Thisstrategycreatesaflywheelthatacceleratestechnological

to adopt such a “dual-leg” strategy and demonstrate its commercialviabilityat scale. For more information

OurLong-standingStrategy:AdvancingFullAutonomy
Sinceourinception,ourobjectivehasbeenclear:toachievescalablefullautonomousdriving.
–152–

=== PAGE 162 ===
BUSINESS
To consistently outperform human drivers on safety, an autonomous driving system must be able to
handle a wide range of rare, unpredictable and highly complex real-world driving situations, including
unusual traffic behavior, extreme weather, unexpected road conditions and emergency events. These
situationsarecommonlyreferredtoasthe“cornercases.”
Earlyon, we recognizedthataddressingcornercasesatscalerequiresexposuretomassivevolumesof
real-world driving data, measured in hundreds of billions of kilometers. We also recognized the inherent
limitations of traditional rule-based approaches that rely on predefined, human-written rules. Such
approaches struggle to cope with the complexity and variability of real-world driving, as finite set of rules
can hardly fully anticipate the breadth of human behavior, road conditions and environmental factors
encounteredineverydaydriving.
Asaresult,webelievethatadata-drivenapproach,inwhichsystemslearnfromlarge-scalereal-world
driving behavior, represents a practical and scalable path forward. We also believe that data at this scale is
most effectively accumulated through broad deployment on mass-produced vehicles, rather than through
smalltestfleetsoperatingincontrolledenvironments.
AutonomousDrivingPlatform
Unlike closed, vertically integrated systems, we are building an open, modular and highly
generalizable platform for driving automation, with the goal of becoming the “Android system” of
autonomousdriving.Themodularityandgeneralizationofourplatformsupportseamlessintegrationacross
diversevehiclemodelsandrobotaxi-drivingoperations.Ourplatformhasthreekeyfeatures:
• Openness.Wefollowanopenplatformapproach,workingcloselywithOEMsandothermobility
platforms to accommodate various development stages and market strategies. Our solutions are
adaptabletodifferenthardwareconfigurations,vehicletypes,priceranges,andfunctionalneeds.
• Modularity. We have developed a unified platform architecture with standardized interfaces,
ensuring consistent user experience and system compatibilityacross different vehicle models and
hardwaresetups,whileenablingfastdeploymentatscale.
• Generalization. We use a “map-free” approach, which allows our systems to operate anywhere
there are roads, without relying on pre-built HD maps. This provides strong geographical
adaptabilityandmakeslarge-scaledeploymentpossible.
Real-WorldDataFoundation
Real-world driving data serves as the foundational input for our model training. We believe that
training autonomous driving models using large-scale real-world driving data, rather than relying primarily
onsimulationdata,enablesfasterprogresstowardscalableLevel4autonomousdrivingcapabilities.
Real-world deployment continuously exposes our systems to naturally occurring traffic conditions
across diverse operating environments, including rare or unpredictable events. We believe such large-scale
real-world driving data is a key determinant of model performance, a view supported by academic and
industry research. Simulation environments, by design, rely on predefined assumptions and modeled
conditions and therefore may not fully capture the full variability, statistical distributions or edge cases
encountered in real-world driving. For this reason, simulation is highly effective when built upon
representative real-world data. In our development process, simulation complements real-world training by
improvingtestingefficiencyandenablinglarge-scalevalidation.
Real-world driving data captures complex interactions among vehicles, pedestrians and other road
users, as well as environmental and sensor effects such as glare or partial obstruction that are difficult to
model comprehensively in simulated environments. Training and validating our systems using operational
road data allows us to refine perception and decision-making models under safety-critical conditions and
acrossawiderangeofreal-worldsituations.
–153–

=== PAGE 163 ===
BUSINESS
Our deployment strategy further creates a continuous feedback loop. Data generated from mass-
produced vehicles in operation is incorporated into subsequent model training and system updates, which
are then redeployed and further improved through additional real-world driving. As deployment scale
increases,thisiterativecycleacceleratessystemlearningandsupportsthegradualexpansionofautonomous
drivingcapabilitiestowardscalableL4deployment.
Data-DrivenAlgorithm
Since entering mass-production in 2022, our data-driven core model has undergone six generations of
iteration. Its fifth generation, AD Algorithm 5.0, introduced an end-to-end AD algorithm that integrates
perception and decision-making within a unified framework. Rather than relying on modular pipelines or
manually engineered intermediate steps, the system learns driving behaviors directly from large-scale real-
worlddrivingdata,enablingmoreconsistentandreliableperformanceincomplexoperatingenvironments.
Reinforcement-learning is emerging as a key enabler for scalable full autonomy. With sufficient
compute and data, reinforcement-learning can allow AI systems to achieve human-level performance and,
in certaintasks, exceeditbyasignificantmargin.In thedrivingautomationindustry, accordingtoCIC, we
are the first independent driving automation solutions provider globally to deploy a reinforcement-learning
largemodel,theR6ReinforcementLearningLargeModel(the“R6Model”),inmass-producedvehicles.
In contrast to the previous generation, AD Algorithm 5.0, which primarily adopted imitation learning
by mimicking experienced human drivers and, while still delivering solid performance, was fundamentally
constrained by the upper bound of human performance, the R6 Model removes this limitation by learning
within world environments that encompass diverse simulated driving trajectories. Each trajectory is
evaluated against multiplereward functions covering safety, comfort, and efficiency,enablingthe modelto
continuouslyoptimizedecision-makingbyreinforcingoptimalbehaviorsandpenalizingsuboptimalones.
A key advantage of the R6 Model lies in its ability to leverage both good and bad data: high-quality
behaviorisstrengthenedthroughpositiverewards,whilepoorbehaviorisexplicitlypenalized,maximizingthe
valueofdatageneratedbymass-producedvehiclesafterSOP,whereeverykilometerdrivenbecomespotential
traininginput.Accordingtoourinternaltestingdata,theR6Modelachievesperformanceimprovementsofup
toapproximatelyeighttimesincertainsafety-criticalscenarioscomparedwiththepreviousgeneration.
Supported by reinforcement-learning, the R6 Model delivers notable improvements in safety,
compliance with traffic regulations, and more driving automation decisions. Up to now, the R6 Model has
already been deployed in mass-produced vehicles, including the Buick Electra L7 under SAIC-GM and
Chery’s Fulwin T11, and we plan to equip future vehicle models with the R6 Model. As its reinforcement-
learning-driven characteristics translate into more stable, comfortable and human-like driving behavior in
real-world use, the resulting improvement in user-perceived driving performance has become increasingly
visible, as reflected in driver reviews and usage feedback shared on major social media platforms. Such
marketfeedbackprovidesadditionalevidenceoftheR6Model’simpactonend-userdrivingexperienceand
serves as a relevant reference point for OEMs in evaluating and positioning the R6 Model as a
differentiatingdrivingautomationconfigurationintheirvehicles.

These vehicles collect large volumes of real-world data, which improve our algorithms and, in turn, support
ourSolutionsforRobotaxiServices.TheadvancementsmadeinRobotaxitechnologyfeedbackintoSolutions
forMass-producedVehicles,creatingacontinuouscycleofimprovementinbothsegments.
This strategy is commercially and technologically distinct because it combines Solutions for Mass-
produced Vehicles and Solutions for Robotaxi Services on the same platform, whereas many competitors

Data-Driven and Map-Free: A Faster and Distinctive Path to the Commercialization of Solutions for
RobotaxiServices
Wearecommittedtoadata-drivenandmap-freetechnologypath,whichwebelieveoffersafasterand
more scalable route to commercializing Robotaxi services than traditional approaches. Many legacy
Robotaxi programs rely on two upfront steps before meaningful rollout: first, building and constantly
maintainingdetailed, city-specifichigh-definitionmaps, and second, operatinglarge, dedicatedLevel4 test
fleets to collect sufficient driving data. Both steps are capital-intensive and slow to scale, and high-
definition maps in particular require continual updates and can lag real-world changes, constraining
deploymentspeedandcoverage.
We strategically pioneered a different path. Our strategy of Solutions for Robotaxi Services is built
aroundamap-freeframeworkthatlearnsdirectlyfromlargevolumesofreal-worlddrivingdata.Inpractice,
the data generated by mass-produced vehicles equipped with our solutions feeds into the development and
validation of our Level 4 capabilities. Because these systems share a common software base and broadly
similarhardwareconfigurations,datacollectedfrommass-marketdeploymentscanbeusedforhigher-level
automation with limited additional processing. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle: broader deployment
yields more real-world experience, which improves performance, reduces dependence on dedicated test
fleetsandhigh-definitionmaps,andacceleratesexpansionintonewcities.
Accordingly, scaling Robotaxi services into a sustainable commercial business requires three factors:
the ability to operate safely in complex and infrequent driving situations, the ability to expand quickly
–156–

=== PAGE 166 ===
BUSINESS
across different cities, and a cost-efficient structure that supports large-scale rollout. Our approach is
designedaroundthesethreerequirementsanddeliversthreecorrespondingadvantages:
• Data Advantage: Solving Corner Cases with Real-World Driving Data. Scaling Robotaxi
operations depends on safety, which is driven by the algorithm’s ability to handle rare,
unexpected corner cases, i.e. situations that occur infrequently but are critical for safety. Unlike
rule-based systems, which struggle to cover all possible scenarios, our data-driven approach
continuouslyrefinesmodels,adaptingtonewandunforeseensituations.Byleveraginglargefleets
of mass-produced vehicles, we expose our models to billions of kilometers of real-world driving
data, far outpacing competitors, according to CIC. We believe real-world driving data provides a
more reliable basis for model development than simulation alone because it reflectshow vehicles
actually operate on the road, including complex or uncommon situations that are difficult to fully
recreate in simulations. From this data, we identify high-value “Golden Data,” which refers to
driving data that is particularly useful for improving the autonomous driving algorithm. Not all
driving data has the same value, and much of real-world driving is routine and repetitive,
supportingbasicsystemstabilitybutaddinglimitedlearningvalueoncethesepatternsarelearned.
By contrast, Golden Data captures difficult situations and high-quality human driving behavior
that meaningfully improves the system’s real-world decision-making. With minimal marginal
costs, thisdata-drivenmodelcreatesasafeandreliableRobotaxisafetysystem,enablingscalable
autonomous fleet operations. For further details, see “—Our Technologies—Massive Real-World
DrivingDataandCornerCases”and“—OurTechnologies—Data-DrivenAlgorithm:End-to-End
BigModelwithReinforcement-Learning.”
• Generalization Advantage: Rapid Expansion without HD Maps. Our map-free technologies
offer a significant advantage in rapid deployment across diverse road environments. Unlike
traditional systems that depend heavily on HD maps, which slow down deployment and
increase costs, our technology allows vehicles toperceiveandmakereal-timedecisions without
relying on HD maps, much like an experienced human driver adapting to new cities or roads.
This means we can launch our Robotaxi services in new cities without the need for time-
consuming and expensive map-building processes. Our system’s ability to adapt to different
environments allows us to scale fleets equipped with our technologies in new markets much
faster,bypassingthelimitationsthatmap-dependentsystemsface.
• CostAdvantage:Efficient,ScalableRobotaxiDeploymentwithMass-producedVehicles.Tomake
Robotaxi services commercially viable, we need a cost-effective model. Unlike other operators
that rely on expensive custom retrofits, our Robotaxi solutions are deployed on mass-produced
vehicles. By leveraging the sensor and hardware platforms of mass-produced vehicles, such as
SAIC’sIMLS6,weensurethatourvehiclesareequippedwithreliable,off-the-shelfsystemsthat
can be easily scaled. Additionally, the use of mass-production significantly reduces per-vehicle
modification costs, allowing us to achieve substantial savings in vehicle assembly and hardware
integration.Withautomotive-gradeverificationanddeepcustomizationduringthepre-production
phase, we ensure high reliability and durability, avoiding costly post-production modifications
and the risks associated with retrofitting. This model is both cost-effective and scalable, allowing
us to expand Robotaxi fleets efficiently while maintaining the long-term reliability needed for
large-scaleoperations.
We are building a common and open “Android-type” ecosystem, rather than a closed system, to enable
the widespread adoption of safe, intelligent and efficient mobility worldwide. With this in mind, we are
building our Solutions for Robotaxi Services around broad partnerships with leading regional mobility

In contrast to the previous generation, AD Algorithm 5.0, which primarily adopted imitation learning
by mimicking experienced human drivers and, while still delivering solid performance, was fundamentally
constrained by the upper bound of human performance, the R6 Model removes this limitation by learning
within world environments that encompass diverse simulated driving trajectories. Each trajectory is
evaluated against multiplereward functions covering safety, comfort, and efficiency,enablingthe modelto
continuouslyoptimizedecision-makingbyreinforcingoptimalbehaviorsandpenalizingsuboptimalones.
A key advantage of the R6 Model lies in its ability to leverage both good and bad data: high-quality
behavior is strengthened through positive rewards, while poor behavior is explicitly penalized, maximizing

OURSOLUTIONS
OurRevenueModel
Our solutions currently include: (i) Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles; and (ii) Solutions for
Robotaxi Services. During the Track Record Period, our revenue contribution was substantially generated
fromourSolutionsforMass-producedVehicles.
SolutionsforMass-producedVehicles
Our revenue model mirrors the commercializationlifecycle of the automotive industry and consists of
twocomponents:(i)pre-mass-productiontechnicaldevelopmentservicefees;and(ii)post-mass-production
licensingfees.
TechnicalDevelopmentServices
A nomination typically occurs when we receive a “letter of intent” or “letter of nomination” from an
OEM indicating its intention to cooperate with us. This is followed by the execution of a formal, legally
bindingcontractwiththeOEM,eitherdirectlyorthroughitsdesignatedtier-1suppliers.Incertaincases,we
may also enter into binding contracts with OEMs without a prior letter of intent. After receiving
nominations and executing customer contracts, we provide technical development services to adapt,
validate, and integrate our solutions into OEMs’ vehicle models intended for mass-production. These
services encompass software customization, model integration, hardware adaptation, and
production-readiness testing. Fees are determined based on project scope and complexity and are typically
recognized progressively prior to SOP, the point at which a vehicle model equipped with our solutions
entersmass-production.
LicensingFees
As a vehicle model advances from nomination and development to SOP and mass-production, we
begin to receive licensing fees from the OEM for the usage of our solutions installed on such mass-
producedvehicle.
In addition, we provide up to five years of free over-the-air updates delivered through our “Momenta
Mainline” framework, as part of our post-sales support. Updates or enhancements outside the scope of the
Momenta Mainline are generally subject to separate charges. We typically provide updates and upgrades at
least twice per year, with the release schedule coordinated with the OEM’s development and production
planning.
Sincewechargelicensingfeesbasedonthenumberofvehiclesequippedwithoursolutions,weexpect
togeneratemorelicensingrevenueasourinstallationvolumecontinuestoincrease,drivenbythesustained
increases in the number of our SOP which, in turn, have been driven by increases in the number of our
OEM customers and nominations, and we anticipate that licensing fees will become a major driver of our
totalrevenueintheforeseeablefuture.AsofDecember31,2025,theinstallationvolumeofoursolutionsin
mass-producedvehiclesexceeded680,000units.

Our technical development services and post-mass-production licensing services are typically
structured and negotiated together as an integrated arrangement. In practice, the objective of the technical
development phase is to achieve SOP for the relevant vehicle model, and the licensing phase is intendedto
apply upon and following SOP. This structure also reflects the technical realities of deploying driving
automation solutions in mass-produced vehicle models. An OEM cannot deploy an driving automation
solution directly into a vehicle platform without first completing the necessary engineering adaptation,
vehicle-level integration, calibration and validation work in collaboration with us. Each vehicle model has
distinctengineeringarchitecture,electronicandelectrical(E/E)configurations,sensor layouts,performance
specifications, and design parameters, which require tailored software adaptation and system-level
optimization. As a result, the technical development phase is a prerequisite to enable subsequent
commercialdeployment.During the Track Record Period, licensingfeeswereprimarilychargeduponSOP
onaper-vehiclebasisasaone-timelicensefee.Ourlicensegrantedhasitsstandalonefunctionality,andwe
recognize a one-off, non-refundable license fee at the point of time when it is installed on our customers’
mass-producedvehicles.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,therewerenocustomersthat,aftercompletionof
the technical development services and commencement of SOP, did not proceed to purchase the
correspondingpost-mass-productionlicensingservices.

reached RMB967.9 million in 2025, and licensing revenues as a percentage of our total revenue has

Looking forward, as the number of vehicles equipped with our solutions continues to grow and we

SolutionsforMass-producedVehicles
OurSolutionsforMass-producedVehiclesinvolvesthedeploymentofoursolutionsinmass-produced
vehicles manufactured by OEMs. These solutions focus primarily on Urban NOA functions, representing a
significant advancement beyond ADAS. Conventional ADAS generally provide isolated assistance for
specific driving tasks, such as maintaining speed or supporting safety functions, while the driver remains
actively engaged in vehicle operation and are not designed for continuous driving across an entire journey
–168–

=== PAGE 178 ===
BUSINESS
or for operationin complexurban environments. In contrast,our solutionsenablecontinuouspoint-to-point
navigationacrosshighwaysandcomplexurbanroadsthroughadvancedcapabilities,primarilyUrbanNOA,
allowingthesystemtoperformmostdrivingtasksthroughoutajourneyunderdriversupervision.UnlikeL3
solutions, drivers remain responsible for supervision and must stay ready to intervene, although active
driverinputduringoperationissignificantlyreduced.
We provide customers with autonomous driving softwaresolutionsanddonotmanufactureor provide
hardware. The underlying hardware platform on which our solutions operate, including system-on-chip
components, driving automation domain controllers and sensors, is supplied to OEMs by third-party
hardware providers. We are responsible for developing the autonomous driving algorithms and adapting
them to each OEM’s selected vehicle model and hardware configuration to enable driving automation
functionalities. We may procure hardware, components and related services from third-party suppliers for
internal purposes, including research and development, testing, validation, system integration and
deploymentsupport.
CoreCompetencies
Our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles are designed to deliver a comprehensive point-to-point
driving experience across highway, urban and parking scenarios. The key functions of our Solutions for
Mass-producedVehiclesaredescribedbelow.
• Urban NOA. Urban NOA provides an end-to-end driving experience on city streets, guiding the
vehicle from the starting point to the destination across complex urban road networks. It is
designed to operate broadly across cities, anytime and anywhere, without reliance on high-
definition maps. Urban NOA is designed to handle challenging urban scenarios, including dense
traffic involving pedestrians, cyclists, scooters and other vulnerable road users, narrow and
irregular roads, and complex intersections, and to operate reliably in both daytime and nighttime
conditions. The system is designed to minimize driver intervention by autonomously handling
mostdrivingtasks,whileensuringthedriverremainsattentiveandreadytotakecontrolifneeded.
We are the first independentUrban NOA solutions provider in China to achievemass-production
ofmap-freeUrbanNOAsolutionswithcountry-widecoverage,accordingtoCIC.
• HighwayNOA.HighwayNOAdeliversasmoothandconsistenthighwaydrivingexperiencewith
system-initiated lane changes and ramp entry or exit maneuvers. It is designed to closely mimic
natural human driving behaviors, especially in complex highway situations such as early lane
changes and merges. With real-time road information and continuous updates, Highway NOA
overcomes the limitations of traditional HD maps that often suffer from outdated or incomplete
data. Covering major highways across the Chinese mainland and other key overseas regions,
Highway NOA provides safe, intelligent, and efficient highway cruising assistance capable of
managingdiverseandchallengingdrivingconditions.
• Super Parking. Super Parking provides comprehensive assistance across multiple scenarios,
incorporating Auto Parking Assist (APA), Remote Parking Assist (RPA), Learned Parking
Navigation Pilot (LPNP), and Parking Navigation Pilot (PNP). Our Super Parking solution has
demonstrated exceptional performance, with three key metrics surpassing the industry average,
including a parking success rate of over 95%, an average maneuver completion time of
approximately 35 seconds, and the capability to operate across more than 300 types of parking
scenarios,accordingtoCIC.
• Others. Our Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles also include other functions designed to
enhance safety, efficiency and user experience, such as adaptive cruise control, lane centering,
user-initiatedlanechanges,autonomousemergencybraking,emergencysteering,andlanesupport
systems,amongothers.

FutureDevelopmentPlan
As our models continue to evolve and improve in performance, we expect our Solutions for
Mass-produced Vehicles to achieve higher levels of automation. This mass-production and scalable
deployment strategy not only supports the scalability of our solutions but also provides a solid foundation
for progressively achieving higher levels of autonomy. By staying at the forefront of technological
advancements, we ensure our solutions remain adaptable, enabling a smooth transition toward fully
autonomousdrivingaswerefineourtechnologyandexpanddeploymentcapabilities.
We are collaborating with leading OEMs on the development of advanced L3 autonomous driving
technologies. Pre-SOP development and OEM acceptance are currently targeted for 2026, with mass-

therelevantOEMprograms.
Our roadmap toward L3 autonomy is underpinned by three core capabilities. First, we employ a
symmetric L3/L4 system design, with key redundancies and architectural features pre-validated through
mass-producedUrbanNOAsolutions,whichmitigatesrisk,acceleratesintegration,andimprovesscalability
as we progress toL3. Second, our R6Modelhas beenvalidatedinmass-productionNOA deploymentsand
continues to advance through iterative learning, providing a credible and measurable path to L3-level
performance. Third, we collaborate closely with global OEMs operating under stringent safety standards,
allowing us to develop early expertise in L3 safety, validation, and homologation requirements while
continuouslyenhancingoursystemandprocessmaturity.
As we advance toward L3, we also plan to further diversify how we monetize our software in order to
better match the way advanced functions are adopted and used over time. Today, we primarily monetize
through a software licensing model, under which we license our solutions to OEMs for integration into
specific vehicle models. The fees are typically agreed upfront for the relevant program and are generally not
linkedtohowfrequentlyindividualendusersactivateorusespecificfunctionsafterdelivery.Buildingonthis
foundation, we plan to introduce an end-user subscription offering for advanced driving automation features.
End users will be able to select flexible purchase options for high-level functions, including urban NOA and
L3-level piloted driving, such as monthly subscriptions, annual renewals, or a one-time perpetual purchase.
This model is expected to complement our existing licensing arrangements by creating recurring end-user
revenueoverthevehiclelifecycle,enhancingtheeconomicvaluepervehicleacrossitsfulllifecycle.

OurPathtoLarge-ScaleDeploymentofSolutionsforRobotaxiServices
As we aim to transition Solutions for Robotaxi Services from pilot projects to a fully scalable
autonomous mobility solution, we expect our strategic plan to unfold in several interlinked stages: current
operationalprogress,scalableexpansion,andcommercialsuccessthroughinnovation.
• Current operational progress: Currently, our Robotaxi operations are in the pilot deployment
phase,operatinginspecificoperationaldesigndomains.Theseinitialdeploymentsareessentialto
refine our technology and gather the necessary data for scaling. While we are still in the early
stages, these operations are critical in building the foundation for expanding to a large-scale
public rollout. Our immediate focus is on optimizing the system and proving the viability of the
modelforpublicadoption.
• Scalable expansion: The next phase involves scaling our operations from pilot programs to full-
scale public adoption. This will require the safe deployment of tens of thousands, eventually
hundreds of thousands, of autonomous vehicles across various real-world environments. To
ensure public confidence and regulatory approval at such a scale, our autonomous systems must
outperform human drivers in terms of safety, typically by an order of magnitude. Given the
currentfatalityrateofoneaccidentper100millionkilometersforhumandrivers,wemustcollect
hundreds of billions of kilometers of data to address rare and high-impactedge cases. To achieve
this, we are moving away from relying solely on proprietary pilot fleets, which would be cost-
prohibitive and time-consuming. Instead, we are creating a scalable data flywheel by leveraging
mass-produced vehicles to gather high-quality driving data, accelerating training, validation, and
continuous safety improvements. This approach allows us to achieve large-scale deployment
fasterandmoreefficiently,positioningusforlong-termsuccess.
• Commercial success through innovation: Our path to scaling L4 autonomy is driven by a data-
centric strategy, embodied in our “One Flywheel, Two-Leg” approach. This strategy integrates a
self-reinforcing data loop with two complementary deployment pathways. It allows us to reuse
sensor configurations from our mass-production vehicles, enabling real-world data from these
vehicles to directly improve and refine our model. This data is diverse and high-quality,
continuously enhancing the safety and performance of our Robotaxi services. As we expand, our
scalable L4 autonomy will be supported by a unified platform that allows us to extend beyond
Robotaxi into other applications like Robovan and Robotruck. By using the same platformfor all
theseservices,weensureoperationalconsistencyandasmoothtransitionaswescale,enablingus
to meet growing demand efficiently while maintaining a unified technological foundation across
applications.

Our Flywheel Approach: Accelerated Performance Enhancement through Automatic, Large-scale
Self-learning
Oneofthemostcriticalchallengesinautonomousdrivingliesinachievingefficientandrapiditeration
tomatchthecomplexityofreal-worlddriving.Weaddressthisthroughourproprietaryflywheelapproach,a
loop that continuously enhances algorithmic intelligence, driving safety, and commercializationscalability.
This approach transforms the vast real-world driving data collected from mass-produced vehicles and
Robotaxifleetsintoapowerfulenginefortechnologicalevolution.
Our flywheel approach is built upon three components: massive real-world driving data generated by
vehiclesequippedwithourdrivingautomationsystems,theautomationtoolchainknownasthe“CLA,”and
our data-driven algorithm, as illustrated by the graphic below. Massive real-world driving data, CLA, and
data-driven algorithm do not operate independently. Instead, they work together as an integrated system:
real-world driving data is continuously collected from mass-produced vehicles and Robotaxi fleets,
processed and prioritized through CLA, used to train and validate our algorithm, and then deployed back
intovehicles—generatingnewreal-worlddrivingdataandacceleratingthenextiteration.
