We believe that progressing from lower-level assisted driving solutions toward L3 and, over time, L4
for mass-produced vehicles represents a practical and scalable path under the current regulatory,
technologicalandcommercialenvironment.Fromaregulatoryperspective,thecommercializationofhigher
levelsofautomationformass-producedpassengervehiclesisproceedinginstagesratherthanbeingopened
to the market all at once. Current L4 deployments are still largely limited to small-scale operations within
designated cities, routes or operational domains, rather than broad-based commercial rollout across mass-
produced passenger vehicles. Against this backdrop, we believe that a progressive pathway from lower-
levelassisteddrivingtohigherlevelsofautonomyismoreconsistentwiththepaceofregulatoryevolution.
From a technological perspective, achieving scalable L4 autonomous driving requires the system not
only to function in controlled settings, but also to perform safely and reliably across an extremely broad
range of complex, rare and continuously evolving real-world conditions. We recognized early on that a
–174–

=== PAGE 184 ===
BUSINESS
data-driven approach, in which algorithms learn from large-scale real-world driving behavior and ongoing
deployment feedback, provides a more practical and scalable path toward that objective. By contrast, an
approachthatseekstopursuehigher-levelautonomyprimarilythroughpredefined,human-writtenrulesand
relativelylimitedtestfleetsisinherentlymoredifficulttoscale,becausethediversityandlongtailofcorner
casesencounteredinreal-worlddrivingcannotbeexhaustivelyanticipatedormanuallyencodedinadvance.
Asthedeploymentbaseofmass-producedvehiclesexpands,thevolumeanddiversityofreal-worlddriving
data also increase, enablingcontinuous algorithmiterationand progressively improvingthe upper bound of
systemsafetyandperformance.
Fromacommercialperspective,themassproductionoflower-levelassisteddrivingsolutionsprovides
a more stable and sustainable revenue base to support the research and development required for higher-
level autonomous driving technologies. This allows technological advancement and commercialization to
reinforce one another, rather than relying solely on long-cycle, capital-intensive development before
meaningful revenue generation. We believe this progression enables us to advance toward L3 and, over
time, L4 in a manner that is more sustainable, more scalable and better aligned with the realities of the
industry’sregulatoryandtechnologicaldevelopment.
MassiveReal-WorldDrivingDataandCornerCases
Ourproprietaryaccesstomassive,high-qualityreal-worlddrivingdataprovidesacriticalandindustry-
leading foundation for the development of AD technologies. We have accumulated massive real-world
driving data across a wide spectrum of scenarios from our own development fleets, mass-produced vehicle
modelsequippedwithoursolutions,andRobotaxifleets.AsofDecember31,2025,theinstallationvolume
of our Solutionsfor Mass-produced Vehicleshadexceeded680,000 units, withcumulativenominationsfor
170 vehicle models, including 68 models that had reached SOP. These vehicles support large-scale data
return,withapproximately630,000clipscollectedperday.
Real-world driving data delivers exceptional quality and reliability. The scale of our mass-produced
vehicle base, together with the diversity of vehicle models and operating environments, supports a broad
and representative coverage of corner cases. As model capability improves, the requirements for data
quality and scenario value increase, and a larger driving exposure is typically required to identify higher-
value corner cases. Our large, mass-produced fleet strengthens our ability to mine and refine such high-
valuecornercasesandcontinuouslyenrichthehigh-valuetrainingdatausedforalgorithmiteration.
Real-world driving data serves as the foundational input for our model training. We believe that
training autonomous driving systems primarily on large-scale real-world driving data, supplemented by
simulation, enables faster progress toward scalable Level 4 autonomous driving capabilities. Real-world
deploymentcontinuouslygenerates diverse driving data across differentcities,vehicleplatformsandtraffic
environments. This continuous data flow allows our algorithms to improve through ongoing training and
iteration, accelerating model development compared with approaches that rely primarily on simulated
environments. As data accumulates from mass-produced vehicles and robotaxi operations, our systems are
exposed to naturally occurring driving situations, including rare or unpredictable events that are difficult to
predefine or reproduce through simulation alone. This exposure is important for addressing long-tail safety
challengesthatarecriticaltoachievinghigherlevelsofautonomy.
In contrast, simulation environments are designed based on predefined assumptions and modeled
conditions and therefore operate within the boundaries of those assumptions. While simulation improves
testing efficiency and enables large-scale validation, it may not fully capture the full variability of
real-world traffic behavior, human interactions or environmental conditions. In contrast, real-world driving
data reflects naturally occurring interactions among vehicles, pedestrians and other road users, as well as
sensor and environmental effects such as glare, weather variation or partial obstruction. Training and
validating our systems under these real operating conditions allows us to refine perception and
decision-making models for safety-critical use cases. Simulation tools remain an important component of
–175–

=== PAGE 185 ===
BUSINESS
our development workflow, primarily enhancing testing efficiency and validation. However, we believe
simulation is most effective when grounded in representative real-world data and used to complement,
ratherthanreplace,real-worldtraining.
The above view is also broadly consistent with recent academic and industry research on end-to-end
and map-free autonomous driving systems. A conference paper titled “Data Scaling Laws for End-to-End
Autonomous Driving”, publishedintheCVPR 2025Workshop onAutonomousDriving, evaluatedanend-
to-end driving architecture using internal driving datasets ranging from 16 to 8,192 hours and reported that
performance improved as dataset size and model capacity increased together, while also highlighting the
importance of targeted data collection and curation for different driving tasks. A research paper titled
“Alpamayo-R1: Bridging Reasoning and Action Prediction for Generalizable Autonomous Driving in the
LongTail”,publishedonthewebsiteoftheNVIDIA AutonomousVehicleResearchGroupandreleasedas
an arXiv preprint in 2025, described training and evaluation on 80,000 hours of driving data collected
across 25 countries and reported that performance improved as training data scale increased, while also
describing a map-free, HD-map-free approach based on raw sensor inputs rather than pre-built HD maps.
These studies are consistent with our view that large-scale and diverse real-world driving data supports the
training, validationand iteration of autonomous driving systems, including map-free approaches. However,
investors should note that we have not independently verified the underlying data, methodology,
assumptions or findings of such third-party research. References to such research are included for
contextual purposes only and should not be construed as an endorsement or validation of our views or of
oursolutions.
According to CIC, our solutions have demonstrated better performance than the industry average
across several measures, including autonomous emergency braking false positive rate, total intervention
frequency, lane change success rate, roundabout passing rate and U-turn success rate. These measures are
used to assess, among other things, driving safety, stability and the ability of the system to handle complex
driving scenarios. For example, our autonomous emergency braking false positive rate is fewer than one
time per million kilometers, compared with approximately three times per million kilometers for the
industry average, and our lane change, roundabout passing and U-turn success rates each exceed 95%,
comparedwithanindustryaverageofaround90%.
Our reinforcement-learning framework further strengthens the role of real-world data by optimizing
driving behavior through feedback derived from actual driving outcomes rather than predefined rules. Data
generated from vehicles in operation is continuously processed and incorporated into subsequent model
training and system updates, which are then redeployedacross fleets to generateadditionalreal-world data.
This learning process enables the system to learn from both successful and suboptimal driving outcomes,
improving its ability to handle edge cases and adapt to dynamic environments. As deployment scale
increases,thisiterativecycleaccelerateslearningefficiencyandenablesourtechnologytogeneralizeacross
multiplevehiclemodelsandoperatingenvironmentswithoutextensivere-engineering.Webelievethisdata-
driven iteration supports the gradual expansion of autonomous driving capabilities toward scalable Level 4
deployment.
ClosedLoopAutomation:Self-LearningProcessAcceleratingInnovationsandIterations
We have developed Closed Loop Automation (“CLA”) to efficiently identify and use Golden Data to
improve our models. It takes raw driving data collected from vehicles, screens and prepares it for training,
andfeedstheresultsbackintomodeltestingandfurtherimprovement.
OurCLAprimarilyconsistsoffourinfrastructurelayers,whichtogethersupportthefulllifecyclefrom
rawreal-worlddrivingdatatomodelimprovementandvalidation.
• Data Infrastructure. Driving data is first filtered and desensitized on the vehicle before upload to
reduce data volume and protect privacy. After the data is uploaded to the cloud, automated tools
screen and clean it, remove low-quality or incomplete records, and identify data that contains
difficult driving situations or high-quality human driving behavior. Limited manual checks are
–176–

=== PAGE 186 ===
BUSINESS
conducted to verify labeling accuracy. The resulting data is then used for model training and
performance evaluation, with quality checks built into each stage to confirm that the data
contributestomeasurablemodelimprovement.
• Training Infrastructure. Algorithm training requires large-scale compute support. Training
infrastructure provides the underlying compute resources for model training and an automated
platform for compute managementand optimization.It is designed to improve trainingefficiency
and stability by increasing compute utilization, reducing failure rates, and shortening iteration
cycles. It also supports cost-effective compute planning and allocation to help manage long-term
computesupplyandcost.
• Simulation Infrastructure. This infrastructure consists of automated simulation testing modules
used to conduct offline evaluation of trained models and assess performance changes after each
iteration.Itcanprovideabroadlibraryofphysical-worldscenariostoidentifyeffectiveparameter
combinationsandgenerateregressioncases,helpingtovalidatetheeffectivenessandreliabilityof
algorithm updates. It is also designed to reduce testing cost and improve testing efficiency by
standardizingsimulationtestingbeforeroadtests.
• Road Test Infrastructure. After simulation testing, updated models are deployed for real-vehicle
testingthroughthisinfrastructure.Itisdesignedas afull-cycletoolchainforroad-testdatareturn.
It can automatically capture takeover and other testing signals on-vehicle, upload them to cloud
storage, support automated labeling, and generate road-test conclusions through automated
dashboards. This supports more efficient road testing and closes the loop by feeding road-test
resultsbackintosubsequentiterations.
By integrating these infrastructure layers, CLA delivers two core benefits. First, it drives substantial
efficiencygains.Unlikeapproachesthatrelyheavilyonmanualdataprocessingandmanualmanagementof
compute and testing, CLA automates key steps across the iteration lifecycle, improving scalability while
lowering the time and cost required for each iteration. Second, it helps select accurate, diverse and
representativetrainingsamplesbyensuringthatthemostvaluabledataandthemostcriticalcornercasesare
prioritizedfortrainingandvalidation,therebyacceleratingalgorithmimprovement.
As we continuouslyinput more insights into our algorithmthrough our CLA, they evolve and become
more efficient, akin to a flywheel that gains speed and momentum with each added burst of energy. Each
iteration strengthens performance, stability and efficiency, reinforcing our flywheel as our deployed base
anddatascaleexpandovertime.
Data-DrivenAlgorithm:BigModelwithReinforcement-Learning
Ourdata-drivenalgorithmformsthefoundationofoursolutionsandenablescontinuouslearningfromreal-
world driving data. In particular, Golden Data plays a critical role in algorithm iteration because it captures
difficultdrivingsituationsandhigh-qualityhumandrivingbehaviorthatcannotbeeffectivelyaddressedthrough
predefined rules or simulation alone. Data from such situations improves the model’s ability to respond to rare
but safety-critical conditions, while high-quality human driving records help the system learn safer and more
reasonabledrivingdecisions.Inpractice,arelativelysmallamountofGoldenDatamaycontributemoretomodel
improvementthanlargevolumesofroutineandrepetitivedrivingdata.
Unlike traditional rule-based approaches that rely on predefined logic and incremental issue-by-issue
adjustments, our algorithm is designed to learn directly from real-world data through automated training,
testing and ongoing refinement. Over time, we have transitioned from multiple standalone perception
models to a unified data-driven end-to-end architecture, allowing perception, prediction and planning
functions to be trained and optimized together. Building on this architecture, we have incorporated
reinforcement learning into our latest generation models to further improve decision-making quality and
iterationefficiencythroughlarge-scalereal-worlddatalearning.

TheR6ModelandItsKeyEnhancements
Our latest generation AD model is the R6 Model, developed based on reinforcement-learning
principles and trained primarily on real-world driving data collectedfrom deployed vehicles, supplemented
by simulations to improve performance in complex and safety-critical scenarios. According to CIC, the R6
Model is the first reinforcement-learning-based autonomous driving algorithm to enter mass-production
among independent driving automation solutions providers globally, marking a major milestone in
autonomousintelligence.TheR6Modelservesasthecorealgorithmicfoundationbehindoursolutions.The
model has already been integrated into multiple new vehicle programs and is being rolled out across our
OEMcustomersviaover-the-air(“OTA”)updates,ensuringcontinuousimprovementandscalabilityacross
differentvehiclemodels.
Reinforcement-learning is emerging as a critical enabler for scalable full autonomy. Building on our
prior AD Algorithm 5.0, which was deployed at scale on our mass-production vehicle base through large-
scaledataaccumulationandclosedloopautomation,theR6Modelinheritsthismass-productionfoundation
andisdesignedtoadvancebeyondhumandrivingperformancebylearningwithinaworldenvironmentthat
simulates a wide range of driving trajectories. Each trajectory is evaluated using multiple reward functions
covering safety, comfort and driving efficiency, allowing the model to continuously optimize its decision-
making by reinforcing optimal behaviors and suppressing suboptimal ones. A key advantage of the R6
Model lies in its ability to leverage both good and bad data from the real world. High-quality behavior is
strengthened through positive rewards, while poor behavior is explicitly penalized. This unlocks the full
value of data generated by our mass-production fleet after SOP: every kilometer driven, regardless of
outcome, becomes potential training data. As a result, fleet scale directly converts into faster learning and
more robust capability growth. The R6 Model delivers higher safety margins, smoother driving behavior
and greater driving efficiency. In certain safety-criticalscenarios, according to our internal testing data, the
R6 Model achievesperformanceimprovementsof up to approximatelyeighttimescomparedwithprevious
generations.Throughcontinuousreinforcement-learning,theR6ModelcontinuestoimproveafterSOPasit
is deployed across additional mass-produced vehicle programs. This learning method not only removes
certain human performance ceiling, but also provides a pathway for autonomous driving systems to
ultimatelysurpassaveragehumandrivingcapabilities.
–178–

=== PAGE 188 ===
BUSINESS
Supported by reinforcement-learning, the R6 Model is designed to achieve driving capability beyond
human drivers and delivers notable improvements in safety, compliance with traffic regulations, as well as
moredrivingautomationdecisions,including:
• Enhanced Safety: Real-world data is crucial for capturing critical safety situations, especially in
emergencies. Based on 70 million golden data refined from 6 billion kms, the R6 Model delivers
an exceptionally high level of safety. Additionally, the R6 Model has demonstrated a significant
improvement in reducing collision risk with vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians and
cyclists. According to our internal testing data, vehicles equipped with the R6 Model
demonstrated more than eight-fold improvement in avoiding potential collision-risk events
involving vulnerable road users compared with previous generations. This makes the R6 Model
saferinurbanenvironments,significantlyreducingtheriskofaccidentsinvolvingvulnerableroad
users.
• Improved Compliance with Traffic Regulations: The R6 Model uses a reward mechanism, which
functions as an internal training and evaluation system that incentivizes compliance with traffic
rules and penalizes violations, to reduce and constrain behaviors that would breach traffic
regulations. In particular, the frequency of solid line violations has been significantly reduced,
representing a fourfold improvement in compliance compared with the previous generations,
accordingtoourinternaltestingdata.Asaresult,theR6Modeldemonstratesenhancedadherence
to traffic rules and more reliable performance in complex traffic environments, including
situationsinwhichhumandriversmayfailtostrictlyobserveroadmarkingsorotherregulations.
• MoreDrivingAutomationDecisions:TheR6Modeldeliversnatural,smoothdrivingperformance
through reinforcement-learning, and is designed to perform at or above the level of experienced
human drivers in real-world conditions. It operates effectively in dynamic, multi-agent
environments where decisions depend on subtle timing, intent and negotiation with other road
users, and intelligently identifies optimal lane-change opportunities in congested traffic while
navigating complex urban intersections with precision. According to our internal testing data, the
R6 Model has significantly reduced unreasonable lane-change behaviors, with performance
approximately 2.5 times better than previous generations and has reduced unnecessary urban
emergency braking events by approximately two times. Together, these enhancements support a
morecomfortablerideexperienceandmoreefficientend-to-endmobility.
With every mile driven by a vehicle equipped with our technology, our algorithm grows smarter and
more advanced. The improvement in our algorithm enhances the performance of our technology and
solutions and delivers greater value to end users. This in turn attracts more OEMs to collaborate with us,
acceleratesdeployment of our technologies, and generates even more valuableinsights. This powerful self-
reinforcingcycleprovidesuswithadistinctcompetitiveadvantageandsupportsthetraininganditerationof
ourreinforcementlearninglargemodel.
Our Momenta Mainline & Three Pillars: Achieving Engineering Adaptability, Efficiency and
Scalability
Our Momenta Mainline Platform is a unified platform that crystallizes our engineering experience
through standardization, process integration and automation, and is designed to apply to both Mass-
production and Solutions for Robotaxi Services. Early in the development of our business, we recognized
that vehicle hardware configurations vary significantly across models. If each project were developed from
scratch, it would create substantial engineering redundancy and repetitive work. As a result, we
intentionally consolidated our early vehicle adaptation experience into a standardized algorithm mainline
and, on a forward-looking basis, built Momenta Mainline Platform around this algorithm mainline to
support rapid and repeatable deployment across both Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles and Solutions
forRobotaxiServices.

MomentaAdaptor
Momenta Adaptor is a set of standardized development processes and automated toolchains distilled
from our vehicle adaptation experience, designed to achieve repeatability at scale, for both Solutions for
Mass-producedVehiclesandSolutionsforRobotaxiServices.
It structures vehicle adaptation into two core stages: a pre-standardized development stage that
typically delivers around 80% to 90% of mainline performance, followed by a focused customization and
alignmentstagethatclosestheremainingperformancegaptomatchmainlinestandards.
Building on best practices from prior programs, Momenta Adaptor progressively decouples and
calibrates key variables such as signals, SoC platforms and basic software through automation, materially
reducingrepetitivemanualeffortandcommunicationfrictions.
This framework improves development efficiency, enhances performance consistency across projects
andunderpinsscalable,high-qualitymass-productiondeployment.
MomentaFramework
Momenta Framework is a standardizedsoftware frameworkthatoperationalizestheMomentaAdaptor
concept at the software layer. Built on our unified data-driven algorithm architecture, it is designed to
–180–

=== PAGE 190 ===
BUSINESS
support efficient and consistent deployment of a single core algorithm across a broad range of our vehicle
programs — covering deployments in both Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles and Solutions for
RobotaxiServices.
In practice, the framework decouples, layer by layer, key software-side variables in mass-production
deployment — including sensor configurations, functional interactions, production-line processes and
domaincontrollerbasicsoftware—andthenrealignsthemwiththemainlinethroughautomatedtoolchains.
This approach smooths platform differences, enabling one core algorithm stack to be adapted across
different hardware and vehicle platforms while maintaininghigh and consistent performance. It also makes
the deployment of unified core algorithm into robotaxis as smooth as the deployment in Mass-production
vehicles.
By building vehicle models on this unified framework and a single mainline, we can form a powerful
data feedback loop. Real-world driving data from widely deployed vehicles is seamlessly utilized to train
and refine the algorithm towards L3 and L4. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle: increased scale leads to
richer data, which drives performance improvements, further fueling deployment scale and solidifying our
first-moveradvantage.
MomentaBox
Momenta Box is a standardized hardware development toolkit that embodies the Momenta Adaptor
designphilosophyatthehardwarelevel.
It is built as a plug-and-play toolbox integrating data collection, ground-truth systems, reference
sensors and development/debug platforms, and can be mounted on prototype vehicles and validation
vehiclesquicklyforroadtestingandotherevaluations.
By providing a unified environment for high-efficiency data collection, hardware adaptation and
system validation, Momenta Box significantly improves development and testing efficiency, enhances the
reliabilityofintegrationresultsandacceleratestheoverallmass-productionadaptationprocess.
We believe that Momenta Mainline, together with the Three Pillars, delivers the following key

• High Engineering Adaptability. Momenta Mainline Platform is vehicle-agnostic and SoC-

• Expanding Customer Relationships and Monetization Opportunities. Our future revenues and

wallet share with existing OEM customers. As of December 31, 2025, we had established

engagement model, which involves working with OEMs from early development stages through
mass-production, contributes to long-term customer retention and reduces switching risk once
solutions are integrated into mass-production models. Leveraging our unified technology
platform, we are able to deploy solutions across multiple vehicle models within an OEM group
more efficiently, supporting incremental revenue growth without a commensurate increase in
costs. We expect future revenue growth to be driven by broader adoption of our solutions across
additional vehicle models, higher production volumes, and the progression of OEM models from
developmenttomass-production.

SalientTermsoftheAgreementswithourOEMCustomers
The agreements governing the purchase of our solutions and the related technical support by OEMs
typicallyincludethefollowingprovisions:
• Roles and responsibilities. The respective roles and responsibilities of the OEM and us are
generally allocated as follows: (i) we conduct adaptation and development of the driving
automation software for the OEM’s specific vehicle model, including road testing, in accordance
with the scope of work and timeline agreed under the relevant statement of work; (ii) the OEM
provides the resources, materials, information, documentation and development vehicles
necessary for the software development and integration process; and (iii) following the SOP, we
provide post-sales support and standard post-sales warranty in respect of our solutions in
accordancewiththecontractualarrangements.
• Pricing. For Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles, pricing generally comprises (i) technical
development service fees and (ii) post-mass-production licensing fees. We determine the pricing
of these two components based on a range of factors, including project scope, technical
complexity, development resources required, the duration of the vehicle model’s lifecycle,
expectedproductionvolume,commercialarrangementswithOEMcustomersandoverallstrategic
cooperationconsiderations.
• Payment term. Development fees are generally payable in installments by reference to agreed
development milestones, while license fees are typically calculated and settled based on the
numberofvehiclesequippedwithoursolutions.Technicaldevelopmentfeeservicespaymentsare
typicallytiedto agreed developmentmilestones. Such milestonesaredeterminedonaproject-by-
project basis through commercial discussions between us and the OEM, taking into account the
scope and complexity of development work and the expected mass-production timeline of the
relevantvehiclemodel.
–190–

=== PAGE 200 ===
BUSINESS
• Scope and term of license. We typically grant our customers the right to use our solutions on
specified mass-produced vehicle models, with the license term generally running from the
commencementofmass-productionoftherelevantmodeluntiltheendofitslifecycle.
• Delivery, inspection and acceptance. The agreements set out a detailed delivery schedule, and
upon receipt of the deliverables, our customers conduct inspection and complete acceptance
withinareasonableperiodbasedonpre-agreedacceptancestandards.
• Post-sale services. We generally provide standard post-sale support and maintenance services.
Our after-sales support generally includes (i) remediation of defects and vulnerabilities in the
driving automation software, (ii) software updates for a specified period following the
commencement of mass production, and (iii) consultation services relating to the operation and
use of the driving automationsolutions. After the expiry of the warranty period, unless otherwise
agreed between the parties, we are generally not obliged to provide maintenance services or
technicalsupporttocustomers.
• Warranty and Liability. If technical development does not achieve the agreed specifications,
responsibility is determined based on the cause of the issue. We are not responsible where the
issueresultsfromtheOEMortheOEM’sothersuppliers.Wheretheissueisattributabletous,we
aregenerallyrequiredtoimplementremedialmeasuresas providedundertherelevantagreement.
Specifically, if an accident or malfunction is determined to have resulted from defects in the our
solutions, the OEM generally compensates the end user first, and then we will indemnify the
customerfortheresultinglosseswithinthescopeagreedundertherelevantcontract.
• Termination. The agreements may be terminable upon, among others, any material breach that
frustratesorrendersimpossiblethepurposeofthecontract.
During the Track Record Period, we did not experience any returns or rejections from our customers
upondeliveryorpenaltiespaidtocustomersforlatedeliveryorfailureindelivery.DuringtheTrackRecord
Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not experienced any material customer complaint or
productrecallinrelationtoourproductsorservices.

WehavemaintainedbusinessrelationshipswithCustomerEandCustomerGintheordinaryandusual

models entering the SOP and post-SOP licensing stages sooner than those of many other customers. As
licensing revenue generally carries a higher gross profit margin than technical development services, a
higher proportion of licensing revenue from these customers contributed to their relatively higher gross
profitmargins.
Transactions with Customer E and Customer G were conducted on normal commercial terms,
negotiated on an arm’s-length basis, and settled in accordance with the agreed payment and delivery
arrangements. The pricing for both sales and purchases was determined with reference to factors including
technical specifications, project requirements, prevailing market conditions and commercial negotiations,
andwasnotinfluencedbytheoverlappingnatureoftherelationship.
To the best of our knowledge, the overlapping customer–supplier relationship did not result in any
preferential treatment, special terms or concessions beyond those available to our other customers or
suppliers. We believe that such overlapping relationship did not adversely affect our operations, pricing
practicesorindependenceinourbusinessdealingsduringtheTrackRecordPeriod.

ESG (including climate-related) risks and opportunities into our overall risk management framework,
allowing us to proactively identify and address them, thereby strengthening our business resilience and
fosteringlong-term,sustainablevalue.
Board of Directors (Decision-Making Tier) oversees the Company’s material ESG risks and
opportunities. It fulfills this duty by convening board meetings to review and approve the Company’s
ESG strategy, targets, management policies, and approaches, and by overseeing progress towards these
targetsandthedisclosureofrelatedinformation.

ResponsetoClimateChange
We actively support China’s “Dual Carbon” strategy and place great importance on assessing the
potential impacts of climate change on our financial performance and sustainable development. Through
systematic policy research and operational analysis, we will initiate the process of identifying risks and
opportunities related to climate change. Based on this assessment, we will formulate targeted strategies to
effectively manage climate risks while actively seizing the development opportunities presented by the
greentransition.
• Physical risks: Extreme weather events such as typhoons, torrential rain, and flooding pose
physical risks to our operations and could result in adverse financial impacts. Such events could
cause direct damage to our offices, leading to operational suspensions or physical harm to our
employees. They could also disrupt our supply chain, thereby affecting our normal business
operations. To mitigate these risks, we have established a Management System and Process for
Typhoon Risks. This defines key personnel and their responsibilities and sets out emergency
procedures based on typhoon warning signals, including a checklist of necessary emergency
supplies. Through this early warning mechanism and emergency response plan, we continuously
enhanceourresiliencetoextremeweathertominimizefinanciallosses.
• Transition risks: As a developer of driving automation software for new energy vehicles
(NEVs),wefacethefollowingclimatetransitionrisks:Thefirstclimatetransitionrisksarepolicy
and regulation change risks. Changes in policies and regulations, such as the phasing out of
subsidies or the tightening of technical standards, could suppress market demand and increase
compliance costs. The second climate transition risks are rapid technological iteration risks.
Failure to keep pace with industry innovations or algorithm advancements could diminish
technological competitiveness. The third climate transition risks are market risks from
intensifying competition and slower-than-expected industry growth, which may constrain profit
margins and growth potential. Our strategy to mitigate these risks centers on continuous
innovation,forward-lookingpolicyanalysis,androbustESGpractices.
• Opportunities: We see significant climate-related growth opportunities driven by favorable
policies, market expansion, and the role of technology in enhancing energy efficiency, and the

ProtectionofEmployeeRights
In compliance with the Labor Law of the People’s Republic of China and the Labor Contract Law of
the People’s Republic of China, as well as other relevant legal provisions, we have instituted standardized
and compliant management systems covering employee recruitment, compensation and benefits, and
performance evaluation, thereby protecting the lawful rights and interests of our workforce. Through labor
contracts, we rigorously verify the identity, age, and background information of all candidates. We are
firmly committed to prohibiting child labor and any form of forced labor, ensuring that the recruitment
process is based on mutual agreement and that our procedures are both compliant and transparent. From
2023 to 2025, our employee turnover rates were 17%, 21%, and 17%, respectively. We are dedicated to
fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment. In our recruitment process, we prohibit any
discrimination based on gender, ethnicity, race, region, religious belief, or other factors, guaranteeing that
allqualifiedcandidateshaveequalemploymentopportunities.
We value the role and contributions of female employees, ensuring equal treatment for female
employees in various aspects such as career development opportunities, training, and development, and
supporting the growth and advancement of female employees. Besides, we continuously take measures to
promote gender diversity at every organizational level. The Board of Directors currently consists of
12directors,including4femaledirectors.

take timely corrective action in compliance with applicable laws and regulations, should the relevant

RISKMANAGEMENTANDINTERNALCONTROL
Wehaveestablishedandcurrentlymaintainriskmanagementandinternalcontrolsystemsconsisting
of policies and procedures that we consider to be appropriate for our business operations, and we are
committed to continuously enhancing these systems as our business develops. Our Board is responsible
–213–

=== PAGE 223 ===
BUSINESS
for the overall establishment and periodic review of our internal control framework, while senior
management is responsible for the day-to-day implementation and monitoring of internal control
measuresacrossoursubsidiariesandfunctionaldepartments.
In preparation for the Global Offering, we have engaged an independent third-party consultant (the
“Internal Control Consultant”) to perform a review over selected areas of our internal controls over
financial reporting (the “Internal Control Review”) covering the period from October 1, 2024 to
September 30, 2025. The Internal Control Review was conducted from November 19 to December 12,
2025, and a follow-up review (the “Follow-up Review”) was conducted from December 15 to 24, 2025.
Such engagement constituted a long form report engagement pursuant to the relevant technical bulletin
AATB1 issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants. The scope of the Internal
Control Review was agreed in advance among us, the Joint Sponsors and the Internal Control Consultant,
and covered selected entity-level controls and business process-level controls, including, among others,
revenue and receivables, purchases and payables, payroll, asset management, treasury, financial reporting
and taxation, general IT controls (financial reporting-related systems), investment management, insurance,
research and development and intellectual property management. The Internal Control Consultant
conducted the Follow-up Review from December 15 to 24, 2025, to assess the remediation status of the
review findings. The Internal Control Consultant noted that the remediation measures had been
implemented and had no further recommendations as of the date of the Follow-up Review. The internal
controlreviewwas conductedbasedoninformationprovidedbyusandnoassuranceoropiniononinternal
controls was expressed by the Internal Control Consultant. On this basis, our Directors are of the view that
the measures adopted for enhancing our internal control over financial reporting are adequate and effective
inthiscontext.
Wealsomaintaininternalcontrolsoverkeyaspectsofouroperations,including:(i)financialreporting
and treasury management, supported by written accounting and budget policies, approval procedures and
periodic management review; (ii) information security and data protection, including access controls based
ontheprincipleof leastprivilege,encryptedtransmissionandstoragemeasures(asapplicable),backupand
recovery arrangements, and incident response procedures; (iii) human resources and business conduct,
including an employee code of conduct, confidentiality obligations, and internal reporting channels for
suspected misconduct; and (iv) regulatory compliance and contract management, including designated
personnel responsible for monitoring relevant legal and regulatory developments and internal review
proceduresforkeycontractsandcompliancematters.
We will continue to review and improve our risk management and internal control systems to support
ourbusinessgrowthandongoingcompliancerequirements.

CORPORATEGOVERNANCE
Our Company is committed to achieving high standards of corporate governance with a view to
safeguarding the interests of our Shareholders. Our Directors recognize the importance of incorporating
elementsofgoodcorporategovernanceinthemanagementstructuresandinternalcontrolproceduresofour
Groupsoastoachieveeffectiveaccountability.
Under paragraph C.2.1 of part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code, the roles of chairman and chief
executive should be separate and should not be performed by the same individual. Mr. Cao is the
chairperson of our Board and our chief executive officer. With considerable experience in the technology
sector, and having served in our Group since its inception, Mr. Cao has been in charge of the overall
corporate and business strategies of our Group. Despite the fact that the roles of the chairperson of our
Board and our chief executive officer are both performed by Mr. Cao, which constitutes a deviation from
paragraph C.2.1 of part 2 of the Corporate Governance Code, our Board considers that vesting the roles of
the chairperson of our Board and our chief executive officer both in Mr. Cao is beneficial to the
managementofourGroup.ThebalanceofpowerandauthorityisensuredbytheoperationofourBoardand
our senior management, which comprises experienced individuals. Upon Listing, our Board will comprise
five executive Directors, three non-executive Directors and four independent non-executive Directors, and
therefore,willhaveastrongindependenceelementinitscomposition.

WEIGHTEDVOTINGRIGHTSSTRUCTURE
Our Company has adopted a WVR structure, effective upon Listing, to enable the WVR Beneficiaries
to exercise voting control over our Company. This will enableour Companytobenefitfromthecontinuing
visionandleadershipoftheWVRBeneficiarieswhowillcontrolourCompanywithaviewtoitslong-term
prospects and strategy, and is in the best interests of our Company and its Shareholders as a whole. Under
our WVR structure, our share capital comprises Class A Ordinary Shares and Class B Ordinary Shares.
Each Class A Ordinary Share entitles the holder to exercise one vote, and each Class B Ordinary Share
entitlestheholdertoexercisetenvotes,respectively,onmatterssubjecttovotingatgeneralmeetingsofour
Company, subject to Rule 8A.24 of the Listing Rules that requires the Reserved Matters to be voted on a
one-vote-per-share basis. The Reserved Matters are (i) any amendment to the Memorandum and the
Articles, (ii) the variation of the rights attached to any class of Shares, (iii) the appointment, election or
removal of an independent non-executive Director, (iv) the appointment or removal of our Company’s
auditors,and(v)thevoluntaryliquidationorwinding-upofourCompany.
In addition, Shareholders, including holders of Class A Ordinary Shares, holding not less than
one-tenth of the paid-up capital of the Company that carries voting rights at general meetings (on a
one-vote-per-sharebasis)areentitledtoconveneanextraordinarygeneralmeetingofourCompanyandadd
resolutions to the meeting agenda. See “Summary of the Constitution of Our Company and the Company
Laws of the Cayman Islands — 2 Articles of Association” in Appendix III to this prospectus for further
details.
Prospective investors are advised to be aware of the potential risks of investing in companies with
weighted voting rights structures, in particular that interests of the WVR Beneficiaries may not necessarily
always be aligned with those of our Shareholders as a whole, and that the WVR Beneficiaries will be in a
position to exercise their higher voting power to influence the affairs of our Company and the outcome of
Shareholders’ resolutions, irrespective of how other Shareholders vote. Further, prospective investors
should make the decision to invest in our Company only after due and careful consideration. For further
information about the risks associated with the WVR structure adopted by the Company, see “Risk Factors
— Risks Related to the WVR Structure” in this prospectus. Save for the weighted voting rights attached to
Class B Ordinary Shares, the rights attached to both classes of Shares are identical.For further information
about the rights, preferences, privileges and restrictions of the Class A Ordinary Shares and Class B
Ordinary Shares, see “Summary of the Constitution of Our Company and the Company Laws of the
CaymanIslands—2ArticlesofAssociation”inAppendixIIItothisprospectus.

OVERVIEW
We are a leading independent driving automation solutions provider in terms of both technological
advancementandcommercialsuccess.
We operate two solutions: (i) the deployment of our solutions in mass-produced vehicles (“Solutions
forMass-produced Vehicles”)and(ii)thedevelopmentofascalable,driverlessADmobilityandlogistics
business (“Solutions for Robotaxi Services”), with potential expansion into Robovan and Robotruck
services. During the Track Record Period, our revenue contribution was substantially generated from our
Solutions for Mass-produced Vehicles. While we believe Solutions for Robotaxi Services represent an
emergingsource of meaningfulrevenue potentialas the technologycontinues to matureanditscommercial
applicationsexpand.
DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,weexperiencedsignificantgrowthinourfinancialperformance:
• Revenue Growth: Our revenues increased by 78.4%, from RMB742.7 million in 2023 to
RMB1,324.7millionin2024,andfurtherincreasedby82.1%toRMB2,412.5millionin2025.
• Gross Profit: Our gross profit was RMB130.1 million, RMB649.4 million and
RMB1,726.8millionin2023,2024and2025,respectively.
• Adjusted Loss for the Year (Non-IFRS Measure): Our adjusted loss for the year (non-IFRS
measure) was RMB1,093.0 million, RMB959.2 million and RMB302.8 million in 2023, 2024
and 2025, respectively. This represents an adjusted loss for the year margin (non-IFRS
measure)of147.2%,72.4%and12.6%,respectively.

ExpandingOurCustomerBaseandStrengtheningCustomerRelationships

strong and enduring relationships. This makes it less likely for OEMs to switch to alternative suppliers,
especially after incorporating our solutions into their mass-production programs. The trust built through
these relationships, combined with our capability to rapidly deploy solutions on new vehicle models
based on our Momenta Mainline, positions us exceptionally well to expand our footprint across a wide
range of vehicle models from our existing OEM customers. This dynamic foundation lays the
groundworkforsustainedgrowthandlong-termsuccess.
Our future revenues and profitability also depend on both maintaining and growing these existing
relationships while also attracting new customers. We believe we are well positioned to attract new
customers based on our track record of high-quality and timely deliveries, best-in-class solution
performances,andextensiveexperienceswithdeployingsolutionsonmass-producedvehicles.

ContinuedInvestmentinTechnologyLeadershipandInnovations
Sinceourfounding,wehavemadesubstantialinvestmentsinresearchanddevelopmentasitisthekey
driver of our growth and value creation. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, we recorded research and development
expensesofRMB1,281.1million,RMB1,508.3millionandRMB1,868.9million,respectively.
Our research and development efforts are focused on developing next-generation AD solutions,
refining and enhancing our proprietary algorithms, and accelerating the commercialization of our AD
technologies. A core part of our work is centered on advancing our unified technology platform, the
Momenta Mainline, as well as strengthening the self-learning cycle enabled by our flywheel approach and
AD Algorithm R6 Model. Furthermore, we are investing in the development of our Solutions for Robotaxi
Services business, which plays a key role in enabling our flywheel to ultimately reach full autonomy in
driving.
Lookingahead,weexpectourresearchanddevelopmentexpensestocontinuerisingaswecontinueto
advanceourADtechnology,expandourR&Dteamandallocateadditionalresourcestofurtherimproveour
technologicalcapabilities.
We believe that our ongoing investment in research and development is critical to maintaining a
leadership position in the fast-evolving and highly competitive driving automation solutions market. These
investments allow us to not only stay ahead of industry trends but also push the boundaries of autonomous
drivingtechnology.This,inturn,positionsusforlong-termgrowth,drivingbothrevenueandprofitability.
OurAbilitytoEnhanceOperatingEfficiency
We are committed to enhancing our operating efficiency across every aspect of our business
operations.
Our technological advancements continue to provide us with significant cost benefits. By leveraging
our platform-agnostic Momenta Mainline and the “Three Pillars,” we are achieving significant economies
of scale and scalability. After the upfront substantial investment in developing the Momenta Mainline, the
incremental costs required to adapt it for different OEMs are relatively low. This is because the core
components and software architecture can be largely reused with limited necessary tailoring, rather than
requiringthedevelopmentofentirelynewsolutionsforeachvehiclemodel.Weexpectthatour“unitcosts,”
i.e., the costs associated with developing, testing, validating, and deploying our solutions on a per-vehicle-
modelbasiswillgenerallydecreaseovertime,whichcontributestoourprofitability.
In addition, we have adopted a “two-leg” approach that integrates our Solutions for Mass-produced
Vehicles with our Solutions for Robotaxi Services, allowing them to reinforce each other through shared
real-world driving data and continuous technology iteration, and forming the foundation for scalable
autonomous driving. Through our data flywheel, real-world driving data generated from both mass-
produced vehicles and robotaxi fleets is processed via our automation toolchain and used to continuously
train and iterate our proprietary algorithms, before being redeployed through Momenta Mainline. Within
such cost-effective strategic framework, our flywheel serves as the engine of our technology platform. It
begins with our mass-produced vehicles, and allows us to continuously generate large volumes of real-
world driving data covering diverse corner cases. As model performance advances, system capability and
the driving experience improve accordingly, supporting broader adoption across additional vehicle models
and higher production volumes, which in turn generates more data. Unlike many of our peers who rely on
manually filtering and labeling information, this framework allows us to filter, process, and label large
amounts of real-world driving data and use it to train algorithm at a much faster rate and more cost-
effectively. For more information about Momenta Mainline and the “Three Pillars,” see “Business — Our
Technologies — Our Momenta Mainline & Three Pillars: Achieving Engineering Adaptability, Efficiency
andScalability.”

OurAbilitytoInnovateOurMonetizationModel
Ourfuturefinancialsuccesshingesonourabilitytoevolveourmonetizationstrategies.
Over the years, our commercial model has continued to evolve. In the early stage of our business,
our revenues wereprimarilygeneratedfromproject-baseddevelopmentthatreflectedtheengineeringand
validationworkrequiredbeforeour solutionscouldbedeployedonmass-producedvehicles.Wereceived
fees for the pre-mass-production technical development services provided in connection with these
programs.Asmorevehiclemodelsequippedwithoursolutionsenteredmassproduction,ourrevenuemix
began to shift toward recurring post-mass-production licensing fees linked to vehicles already in
operation. These recurring revenues generally carry higher margins than pre-production services and are
expected to account for an increasing proportion of our total revenue. In addition, as we further expand
the deployment of our solutions, we are workingwithmajor OEMs todevelopsubscription-basedmodels
underwhichwemayshareinsubscriptionfeeschargedtoendusers.

operational capabilities required for scaled deployment, we expect to refine and adopt business models
thatcansupportsustainableRobotaxiServicesoverthelongterm.

DESCRIPTION OF KEY COMPONENTS OF CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF PROFIT OR
LOSS
Revenue
During the Track Record Period, substantially all of our revenues were generated from Mass-
production.
Our revenue model for mass-production solutions generally follows the commercialization lifecycle
of the automotive industry and comprises two components: (i) pre-mass-production technical
development service fees; and (ii) post-mass-production licensing fees. A nomination typically occurs
when we receive a “letter of intent” or “letter of nomination” from an OEM indicating its intention to
cooperate with us. This is typically followed by the execution of a formal, legally binding contract with
the OEM, either directly or through its designated Tier-1 suppliers. In certain cases, we may also enter
into binding contracts with OEMs without a prior letter of intent. After receiving nominations and
executing customer contracts, we provide technical development services to adapt, validate, and integrate
oursolutionsintoOEMvehiclemodelsintendedformass-production.Theseservicesencompasssoftware
customization, model integration, hardware adaptation, and production-readiness testing. Fees are
determined based on project scope and complexity and are typically recognized progressively prior to
SOP, the point at which a vehicle model equipped with our solutions enters mass-production. Following
an SOP, we begin to receive licensing fees from OEMs for the usage of our solutions installed on their
mass-producedvehicles.
From a revenue recognition perspective, we recognize revenue only upon entering into formal,
legally binding contracts with OEMs. Technical development service revenue is recognized over time
prior to SOP as the related performance obligations are fulfilled, while licensing service revenue is
recognized only after a licensing agreement has been executed its license granted has its standalone
functionality, and it recognizes a one-off, non-refundable license fee at the point of time when it is
installedonourcustomers’mass-producedvehicles.
Currently, our Solutions for Robotaxi Services primarily involve the deployment of robotaxi equipped
with our AD solutions and technologies in collaboration with our business partners. We have initial
commercial operations in Shanghai and Suzhou and have established cooperation frameworks with leading
globalmobilityplatformsandplantolaunchouroverseascommercialrobotaxiservicesinoverseassuchas

increased from 3.1% in 2023 to 22.1% in 2024 and further to 40.1% in 2025 and generally have relatively
higher gross profit, as a substantial portion of the costs associated with delivering its solutions are incurred
duringthedevelopmentstage,oncethesolutionisdeployedinavehiclemodelthatentersmassproduction,

development cycle for vehicle models and decrease the cost associatedwith developing, testing, validating,
anddeployingoursolutionsonapervehicle-modelbasis.
Due to the varying stages at which OEMs test, validate, and adapt our solutions, as well as integrate

developmentservices,mayfluctuate,leadingtovariationsinouroverallgrossprofitmarginsfromperiodto
period.However,weexpectourgrossprofitmargintobenefitfromtheanticipatedgrowthoflicensingfees,
which typically generate higher margins, as well as improvements in scalability through the use of our
vehicle-agnosticMomentaMainlineandthe“ThreePillars.”

PRC
Pursuant to the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (the “EIT Law”), a domestic enterprise established
within the PRC in accordance with the law shall be regarded as a resident enterprise. A resident enterprise
shall be subject to an EIT at 25% on its global income as determined under PRC tax laws and accounting
standards. Our subsidiaries and VIEs are subject to EIT at 25%. A preferential EIT rate shall be applicable
to key industries or projects supported or encouraged. The EIT Law allows qualified High and New
Technology Enterprises (“HNTEs”) to enjoy a preferential EIT rate of 15%. Beijing Momenta obtained
HNTE certificates in 2022 and was entitled to the preferential EIT rate of 15% for a period of three years
startingfrom2022.BeijingMomentarenewedHNTEin2025,andwasentitledtoapreferentialEITrateof
15% for a period of three years starting from 2025. Suzhou Momenta obtained HNTE certificates in 2022
and was entitled to the preferential EIT rate of 15% for a period of three years starting from 2022. Suzhou
Momenta renewed HNTE in 2025, and was entitled to a preferential EIT rate of 15% for a period of three
years starting from 2025. Beijing Chusudu obtained HNTE certificates in 2022 and was entitled to the
preferential EIT rate of 15% for a period of three years starting from 2022, which expired in 2025.
According to the relevant laws and regulations promulgated by the State Taxation Administration of the
PRC, enterprises engaging in research and development activities are entitled to claim 200% of their
research and development expenses incurred as tax deductible expenses when determining their assessable
profitsforthatyear.
DISCUSSIONOFRESULTSOFOPERATIONS
YearEndedDecember31,2024ComparedWithYearEndedDecember31,2025
Revenues
Our revenue increased by 82.1% from RMB1,324.7 million in 2024 to RMB2,412.5 million in 2025.
The substantial increase was mainly attributable to (i) an increase in licensing revenue, driven by a
substantial increase in the number of vehicle models that had reached the SOP stage, from eight as of
December 31, 2023 to 26 as of December 31, 2024 and further to 68 as of December 31, 2025, and (ii) an
increase in technical development service revenue, mainly driven by higher customer demand. Such
demand reflected growing industry demand for enhanced driving automation capabilities amid intensifying
market competition, OEMs’ strategic expansion of driving automation features from premium models to
mid-range models to enhance competitiveness, and continued customer recognition of our delivery
capabilities,as reflectedintheincreaseinour cumulativenominationsfrom31asofDecember31,2023to
106asofDecember31,2024andfurtherto170vehiclemodelsasofDecember31,2025.
CostofRevenueandGrossProfit
Our cost of revenues increased slightly by 1.6%, from RMB675.3 million in 2024 to
RMB685.8millionin2025.
Our gross profit increased significantly from RMB649.4 million in 2024 to RMB1,726.8 million in
2025. Our gross profit margin increased from 49.0% in 2024, to 71.6% in 2025. This was primarily driven
by continued cost optimization, and increasing economies of scale, using our vehicle-agnostic Momenta
Mainline and the “Three Pillars,” as well as by leveraging our existing know-how and experiences gained
frompriornominationsthathavereachedSOP.Thegrossprofitmarginimprovementwasalsoattributedto
increase revenue contribution from licensing revenue, which typically carries a higher gross profit margin,

Foradetailedbreakdownofourprepayments,depositsandotherreceivablesduringtheTrackRecordPeriod,

Under PRC law, only financial institutions may generally engage in lending as a business. However,
PRC law recognizes private lending arrangements among natural persons, legal persons and other
organizations, provided that such arrangements do not fall within the invalidity circumstances under the
Civil Code of the PRC and the applicable private lending rules. During the Track Record Period and up to
theLatestPracticableDate,lendingwasnottheGroup’sprimarybusiness;theinterestratesoftheemployee
loans did not exceed the applicable statutory limit and such loans did not fall within the invalidity
circumstances under the Civil Code of the PRC and the applicable private lending rules; there were no
disputes with the relevant borrowers; and the Group had not been subject to any administrative penalties,
investigations or enforcement actions, nor had it received any regulatory notice, in connection with such
loans. Based on the foregoing, our PRC Legal Adviser is of the view that the Group’s advances to its
employees as described in the preceding paragraph do not violate any mandatory provision of applicable
PRClawsandregulationsinallmaterialrespects.

business operations. These investments were made in short- to mid-term, low-risk wealth management
products, which mainly included structured deposits, high-liquidity money market funds, and structured
notes.
Our investment strategy prioritizes safety, liquidity, compliance and while maintaining a conservative
riskprofile.Wehaveestablishedarobustsetofinternalriskmanagementpoliciesandguidelines,withclear
approval processes and reporting procedures to ensure that investments align with our liquidity and risk
requirements. We balance our daily operational, investment and financing needs with capital returns
through prudent cash planning and appropriate allocation of investment tenors to ensure timely availability
of funds. We also adopt a diversified allocation approach in selecting investment products and financial
institutions to reduce concentration risk in any single product or counter party. Our treasury and capital
management department, composed of members of our finance department with treasury and capital
management expertise, is responsible for our wealth management activities, and their qualifications,
professional expertise, and extensive experience ensure that investment decisions are made prudently with
full consideration of potential risks. Making general investment decisions is under the supervision of our
BoardofDirectors.

expand our business. During the Track Record Period, no dividend was paid or declared by us. Currently,

whether to distribute dividends, subject to certain requirements of Cayman Islands law. Under Cayman
Islands law, a Cayman Islands company may pay a dividend out of either profit or share premium account,
provided that in no circumstances may a dividend be paid if this would result in the company being unable
to pay its debts as they fall due in the ordinary course of business. Even if our Board decides to pay
dividends, the form, frequency and amount will depend upon our future operations and earnings, capital
requirements and surplus, general financial condition, contractual restrictions and other factors that the
Board may deem relevant. As advised by our legal advisor as to Cayman Islands law, notwithstanding that

parameter scale, the training requirements for next-generation AD models are expected to
grow significantly in terms of computing power and data storage capacity. To support these
evolving requirements, we plan to substantially expand our access to high-performance
computing resources over the next five years. Rather than relying on fixed infrastructure

STABILIZATION
Stabilization is a practice used by underwriters in some markets to facilitate the distribution of
securities. To stabilize, the underwriters may bid for, or purchase, the securities in the secondary market
during a specified period of time, to retard and, if possible, prevent a decline in the initial public market
priceofthesecuritiesbelowtheofferprice.Suchtransactionsmaybeeffectedinalljurisdictionswhereitis
permissible to do so, in each case in compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements,
includingthoseofHongKong.InHongKong,thepriceatwhichstabilizationiseffectedisnotpermittedto
exceedtheOfferPrice.
InconnectionwiththeGlobalOffering,theStabilizingManager(oranypersonactingforit),onbehalf
of the Underwriters, may over-allocate or effect transactions with a view to stabilizing or supporting the
market price of the Class A Ordinary Shares at a levelhigher than thatwhich mightotherwise prevailfor a
limited period after the Listing Date. However, there is no obligation on the Stabilizing Manager (or any
person acting for it) to conduct any such stabilizing action. Such stabilizing action, if taken, (a) will be
conductedattheabsolutediscretionoftheStabilizingManager(oranypersonactingforit)andinwhatthe
–301–

=== PAGE 311 ===
STRUCTURE OF THE GLOBAL OFFERING
StabilizingManagerreasonablyregardsasthebestinterestoftheCompany,(b)maybediscontinuedatany
timeand(c)isrequiredtobebroughttoanendwithin30daysofthelastdayforlodgingapplicationsunder
theHongKongPublicOffering.
Stabilization action permitted in Hong Kong pursuant to the Securities and Futures (Price Stabilizing)
Rules of the SFO includes (a) over-allocatingfor the purpose of preventingor minimizingany reductionin
themarketpriceoftheClassAOrdinaryShares,(b)sellingoragreeingtoselltheClassAOrdinaryShares
so as to establish a short position in them for the purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the
marketprice of theClassA OrdinaryShares, (c)purchasing,or agreeingtopurchase, theClassA Ordinary
Shares pursuant to the Over-allotment Option in order to close out any position established under
paragraphs(a)or(b)above,(d)purchasing,oragreeingtopurchase,anyoftheClassAOrdinarySharesfor
the sole purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the market price of the Class A Ordinary
Shares, (e) selling or agreeing to sell any Class A Ordinary Shares in order to liquidate any position
established as a result of those purchases, and (f) offering or attempting to do anything as described in
paragraphs(b),(c),(d)or(e)above.
Specifically,prospectiveapplicantsforandinvestorsintheOfferSharesshouldnotethat:
(a) as a result of effecting transactions to stabilize or maintain the market price of the Class A
OrdinaryShares,theStabilizingManager(oranypersonactingforit)may,inconnectionwiththe

(b) there is no certainty as to the extent to which and the time or period for which the Stabilizing
Manager(oranypersonactingforit)willmaintainsuchalongposition;

selling in the open market may have an adverse impact on the market price of the Class A
OrdinaryShares;
(d) no stabilizing action can be taken to support the price of the Class A Ordinary Shares for longer
than the stabilization period, which will begin on the Listing Date, and is expected to expire on
Sunday, August 2, 2026, being the 30th day after the last day for lodging applications under the
Hong Kong Public Offering. After this date, when no further stabilizing action may be taken,
demand for the Class A Ordinary Shares, and therefore the price of the Class A Ordinary Shares,
couldfall;
(e) the price of the Class A Ordinary Shares cannot be assured to stay at or above the Offer Price by
thetakingofanystabilizingaction;and
(f) stabilizingbidsor transactionseffectedinthecourseof thestabilizingactionmaybemadeatany
price at or below the Offer Price and can, therefore, be done at a price below the price paid by
applicantsfor,orinvestorsin,theOfferShares.

3.1 Basisofconsolidation
The Historical Financial Information incorporates the financial statements of the Company and entities (including structured
entities)controlledbytheCompanyanditssubsidiaries.ControlisachievedwhentheCompany:
• haspowerovertheinvestee;
• isexposed,orhasrights,tovariablereturnsfromitsinvolvementwiththeinvestee;and
• hastheabilitytouseitspowertoaffectitsreturns.
TheGroupreassesseswhetherornotitcontrolsaninvesteeiffactsandcircumstancesindicatethattherearechangestooneor
moreofthethreeelementsofcontrollistedabove.
WhentheGrouphaslessthanamajorityofthevotingrightsofaninvestee,ithaspowerovertheinvesteewhenthevotingrights
are sufficient to give it the practical ability to direct the relevant activities of the investee unilaterally. The Group considers all
relevantfactsandcircumstancesinassessingwhetherornottheGroup’svotingrightsinaninvesteearesufficienttogiveitpower,
including:
• thesizeoftheGroup’sholdingofvotingrightsrelativetothesizeanddispersionofholdingsoftheothervoteholders;
• potentialvotingrightsheldbytheGroup,othervoteholdersorotherparties;
• rightsarisingfromothercontractualarrangements;and
• anyadditionalfactsandcircumstancesthatindicatethattheGrouphas,ordoesnothave,thecurrentabilitytodirectthe
relevantactivitiesatthetimethatdecisionsneedtobemade,includingvotingpatternsatpreviousshareholders’meetings.
Consolidation of a subsidiary begins when the Group obtains control over the subsidiary and ceases when the Group loses
controlofthesubsidiary.Specifically,incomeandexpensesofasubsidiaryacquiredordisposedofduringtheyearareincludedin
theconsolidatedstatementsof profit or lossandothercomprehensiveincomefrom thedatetheGroupgainscontroluntilthedate
whentheGroupceasestocontrolthesubsidiary.
Profit or loss and each item of other comprehensive income are attributed to the owners of the Company and to the
non-controlling interests. Total comprehensive income of subsidiaries is attributed to the owners of the Company and to the
non-controllinginterestsevenifthisresultsinthenon-controllinginterestshavingadeficitbalance.
Whennecessary,adjustmentsaremadetothefinancialstatementsofsubsidiariestobringtheiraccountingpoliciesinlinewith
theGroup’saccountingpolicies.
Allintragroupassetsandliabilities,equity,income,expensesandcashflowsrelatingtotransactionsbetweenmembersofthe
Groupareeliminatedinfullonconsolidation.

3.6 Governmentgrants
Government grants are not recognized until there is reasonable assurance that the Group will comply with the conditions

Government grants related to income that are receivable as compensation for expenses or losses already incurred or for the

3.7 Employeebenefits
Retirementbenefitcosts
InaccordancewiththerulesandregulationsinthePRC,thePRCbasedemployeesoftheGroupparticipateinvariousdefined
contributionretirementbenefitplansorganizedbytherelevantmunicipalandprovincialgovernmentsinthePRCunderwhichthe

employees’salaries.Paymentstodefinedcontributionretirementbenefitplansarerecognizedasanexpensewhenemployeeshave
renderedserviceentitlingthemtothecontributions.
Short-termemployeebenefits
Short-term employee benefits are recognized at the undiscounted amount of the benefits expected to be paid as and when
employees rendered the services. All short-term employee benefits are recognized as an expense unless another IFRS Accounting
Standardrequiresorpermitstheinclusionofthebenefitinthecostofanasset.
A liability is recognized for benefits accruing to employees(such as wages and salaries) after deducting any amount already
paid.

40. CAPITALRISKMANAGEMENT
TheGroupmanagesitscapitaltoensurethatentitiesintheGroupwillbeabletocontinueasagoingconcernwhilemaximizing
the return to shareholders through the optimization of debt and equity balances. The Group’s overall strategy remains unchanged
fromprioryears.
The capital structure of the Group consists of net debt, which includes the borrowings disclosed in Note 28, lease liabilities
disclosedinNote27,thePreferredSharesdisclosedinNote30,netofcashandcashequivalentsandequityattributabletoownersof
theCompany,comprisingissuedsharecapital,otherreserve,accumulateddeficitandtranslationreserve.
The management of the Group reviews the capital structure regularly. As part of this review, the management of the Group
considersthecostofcapitalandtherisksassociatedwitheachclassofcapital.Basedonrecommendationsofthemanagement,the
Groupwillbalanceitsoverallcapitalstructurethroughthepaymentofdividends,newsharesissuesaswellasraising,extensionand
earlyrepaymentofborrowings.

3. COMPANYLAWSOFTHECAYMANISLANDS
The Company was incorporated in the Cayman Islands as an exempted company on September 19,
2016 subject to the Companies Act. Certain provisions of the company laws of the Cayman Islands are set
out below but thissectiondoes notpurporttocontainallapplicablequalificationsandexceptionsor tobea
complete review of all matters of the company laws of the Cayman Islands, which may differ from
equivalentprovisionsinjurisdictionswithwhichinterestedpartiesmaybemorefamiliar.
3.1 CompanyOperations
An exempted company such as the Company must conduct its operations mainly outside the
Cayman Islands. An exempted company is also required to file an annual return each year with the
Registrar of Companies of the Cayman Islands and pay a fee which is based on the amount of its
authorizedsharecapital.

A company must cause proper records of accounts to be kept with respect to: (i) all sums of

3.9 ExchangeControl
There are no exchange control regulations or currency restrictions in effect in the Cayman
Islands.
3.10 Taxation
The Cayman Islands currently levy no taxes on individuals or corporations based upon profits,
income, gains or appreciations and there is no taxation in the nature of inheritance tax or estate duty.

companiessaveforthosewhichholdinterestsinlandintheCaymanIslands.
3.12 LoanstoDirectors
There is no express provision prohibiting the making of loans by a company to any of its
directors. However, the company’s articles of association may provide for the prohibition of such
loansunderspecificcircumstances.

membersorcorporaterecordsofthecompany.Theywill,however,havesuchrightsasmaybesetout
inthecompany’sarticlesofassociation.
3.14 RegisterofMembers
A Cayman Islands exempted company may maintain its principal register of members and any
branch registers in any country or territory, whether within or outside the Cayman Islands, as the
company may determine from time to time. There is no requirement for an exempted company to
make any returns of members to the Registrar of Companies in the Cayman Islands. The names and
addresses of the members are, accordingly, not a matter of public record and are not available for
public inspection. However, an exempted company shall make available at its registered office, in
electronic form or any other medium, such register of members, including any branch register of
member,asmayberequiredofituponserviceofanorderornoticebytheTaxInformationAuthority
pursuanttotheTaxInformationAuthorityAct(2021Revision)oftheCaymanIslands.

3.16 Windingup
A Cayman Islands company may be wound up by: (i) an order of the court; (ii) voluntarily by
itsmembers;or(iii)underthesupervisionofthecourt.

where,intheopinionofthecourt,itisjustandequitablethatsuchcompanybesowoundup.
Avoluntarywindingupofacompany(otherthanalimiteddurationcompany,forwhichspecific
rulesapply)occurswherethecompanyresolvesbyspecialresolutionthatitbewoundupvoluntarilyor

carryonitsbusinessfromthecommencementofitswindingupexceptsofarasitmaybebeneficialfor
itswindingup.Uponappointmentofavoluntaryliquidator,allthepowersofthedirectorscease,except
sofarasthecompanyingeneralmeetingortheliquidatorsanctionstheircontinuance.

appointedforthepurposeofwindinguptheaffairsofthecompanyanddistributingitsassets.
As soon as the affairs of a company are fully wound up, the liquidator must make a report and
an account of the winding up, showing how the winding up has been conducted and the property of
thecompanydisposedof,andcallageneralmeetingofthecompanyforthepurposesoflayingbefore
ittheaccountandgivinganexplanationofthataccount.
When a resolution has been passed by a company to wind up voluntarily, the liquidator or any
contributory or creditor may apply to the court for an order for the continuation of the winding up
under the supervision of the court, on the grounds that: (i) the company is or is likely to become
insolvent; or (ii) the supervision of the court will facilitatea more effective,economicor expeditious
liquidation of the company in the interests of the contributories and creditors. A supervision order
takes effect for all purposes as if it was an order that the company be wound up by the court except
thatacommencedvoluntarywindingupandtheprioractionsofthevoluntaryliquidatorshallbevalid
andbindinguponthecompanyanditsofficialliquidator.

court, one or more persons may be appointed to be called an official liquidator(s).The court may
appointtosuch officesuch person or persons, eitherprovisionallyorotherwise,asitthinksfit,andif
more than one person is appointed to such office, the court shall declare whether any act required or
authorized to be done by the official liquidator is to be done by all or any one or more of such
persons. The court may also determine whether any and what security is to be given by an official
liquidator on his appointment; if no official liquidator is appointed, or during any vacancy in such
office,allthepropertyofthecompanyshallbeinthecustodyofthecourt.

3.17 MergersandConsolidations
The Companies Act permits mergers and consolidations between Cayman Islands companies and
between Cayman Islands companies and non-Cayman Islands companies. For these purposes, (a)
“merger” means the merging of two or more constituent companies and the vestingof their undertaking,
propertyandliabilitiesinoneofsuchcompaniesasthesurvivingcompany,and(b)“consolidation”means
thecombinationoftwoormoreconstituentcompaniesintoaconsolidatedcompanyandthevestingofthe
undertaking, property and liabilities of such companies to the consolidated company. In order to effect
suchamergerorconsolidation,thedirectorsofeachconstituentcompanymustapproveawrittenplanof
merger or consolidation, which must then be authorized by (a) a special resolution of each constituent
company and (b) such other authorization, if any, as may be specified in such constituent company’s
articles of association. The written plan of merger or consolidation must be filed with the Registrar of
Companies of the Cayman Islands together with a declaration as to the solvency of the consolidated or
survivingcompany,alistoftheassetsandliabilitiesofeachconstituentcompanyandanundertakingthata
copy of the certificate of merger or consolidation will be given to the members and creditors of each
constituentcompanyandthatnotificationofthemergerorconsolidationwillbepublishedintheCayman
IslandsGazette.Dissentingmembershavetherighttobepaidthefairvalueoftheirshares(which,ifnot
agreed between the parties, will be determined by the Cayman Islands court) if they follow the required
procedures, subject to certain exceptions. Court approval is not required for a merger or consolidation
whichiseffectedincompliancewiththesestatutoryprocedures.
3.18 MergersandConsolidationsinvolvingaForeignCompany
Where the merger or consolidation involves a foreign company, the procedure is similar, save
thatwith respect to the foreign company, the directors of the Cayman Islands exemptedcompanyare
requiredtomakeadeclarationtotheeffectthat,havingmadedueenquiry,theyareoftheopinionthat
therequirementssetoutbelowhavebeenmet:(i)thatthemergerorconsolidationispermittedornot
prohibitedbytheconstitutionaldocumentsoftheforeigncompanyandbythelawsofthejurisdiction
in which the foreign company is incorporated, and that those laws and any requirements of those
constitutional documents have been or will be complied with; (ii) that no petition or other similar
proceedinghasbeenfiledandremainsoutstandingorordermadeorresolutionadoptedtowindupor
liquidatetheforeigncompanyinanyjurisdictions;(iii)thatnoreceiver,trustee,administratororother
similarperson has beenappointedinanyjurisdictionandisactinginrespectof theforeigncompany,
its affairs or its property or any part thereof; and (iv) that no scheme, order, compromise or other
similar arrangement has been entered into or made in any jurisdiction whereby the rights of creditors
oftheforeigncompanyareandcontinuetobesuspendedorrestricted.
Where the surviving company is the Cayman Islands exempted company, the directors of the
Cayman Islands exempted company are further required to make a declaration to the effect that, having
madedueenquiry,theyareoftheopinionthattherequirementssetoutbelowhavebeenmet:(i)thatthe
foreign company is ableto pay its debts as they falldueandthatthemergerorconsolidatedisbonafide
andnotintendedtodefraudunsecuredcreditorsoftheforeigncompany;(ii)thatinrespectofthetransfer

(a)consentorapprovaltothetransferhasbeenobtained,releasedorwaived;(b)thetransferispermitted

ceasetobeincorporated,registeredorexistunderthelawsoftherelevantforeignjurisdiction;and(iv)that
thereisnootherreasonwhyitwouldbeagainstthepublicinteresttopermitthemergerorconsolidation.

Reconstructions and amalgamations may be approved by (i) 75% in value of the members or
class of members or (ii) a majority in number representing 75% in value of the creditors or class of

creditors, in each case depending on the circumstances, as are present at a meeting called for such
